So reflect on what this statement contains of acknowledgment of the reality of what they were upon, and how that reality became evident to them on that day, and they knew that what they were in during their terms was their share of enjoying one another, and they did not enjoy the worship of their Lord, His knowledge, His oneness, His love, and preferring His pleasure. This is of the same kind as their saying: ﴿If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾; and His saying: ﴿So they acknowledged their sin﴾; and His saying: ﴿So they knew that the truth belongs to Allah﴾; and their parallels.

The point is that His saying: ﴿except as Allah wills﴾ refers to these mentioned people, either exclusively to them or inclusively to them and to the disobedient monotheists. As for its being restricted to the disobedient Muslims apart from these, there is no basis for that.

When a group saw the weakness of this view, they said: The exception refers to the duration of the barzakh and the place of standing, and the weakness of this view has been made clear. Another group saw that the exception refers to another kind of punishment other than the Fire.

They said: The meaning is that you are in the Fire forever, except what Allah wills to punish you with other than it, which is the zamharir (bitter cold). And Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been an ambush, a place of return for the transgressors, remaining therein for ages﴾.

They said: And eternity is not measured in ages (ahqab).

Ibn Mas'ud said concerning this verse: There will certainly come upon Hell a time when its doors will swing, with no one in it, after they have remained in it for ages.

And from Abu Hurayrah something similar, which al-Baghawi reported from them both. Then he said:

Its meaning, according to the Ahl al-Sunnah, is established if it is proven that no one of the people of faith will remain in it. They said: This has been established from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Mas'ud, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar. Harb asked Ishaq ibn Rahawayh about this verse, and he said: I asked Ishaq: "The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord﴾," and he said: This verse covers every threat in the Qur'an. Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: My father said: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Jabir, or Abu Sa'id, or one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: This verse covers the whole Qur'an: ﴿except as your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is Effective of what He intends.﴾

Mu'tamir said: He said: It covers every threat in the Qur'an. Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Balkh, who heard 'Amr ibn Maymun narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: There will certainly come upon Hell a day when its doors will swing, with no one in it, and that is after they have remained in it for ages.

Ubayd Allah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I am not one who does not say that there will come upon Hell a day when no one will remain in it. And he recited His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, having therein sighing and wailing﴾, the verse.

Ubayd Allah said: Our companions used to say: He means by it the monotheists. Abu Ma'n narrated to us, Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah or one of his companions, concerning His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾, he said: This verse covers the whole Qur'an.

Ibn Jarir reported this view in his tafsir from a group of the early generations. He said: Others said: By that is meant the people of the Fire and everyone who enters it. He mentioned the one who said that, then he mentioned the reports which we will mention.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from his father, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir or Abu Sa'id or from a man of the companions of the Messenger of Allah, concerning His saying: "except as your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is Effective of what He intends," he said: This verse covers the whole Qur'an, meaning: wherever in the Qur'an there is "abiding therein," it covers it. He said: I heard Abu Mijlaz say: "His recompense" — if Allah wills, He will overlook His punishment.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, and he mentioned it, and said: And I was told, from al-Musayyib, from one whom he named, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾.

He said: "They will not die, nor will they be removed from it, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills." ﴿They shall not die therein, nor shall they be removed from it, for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills.﴾

He said: God made an exception, and He said: "God's command is that the Fire should consume them."

He said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "There will surely come upon Hellfire a time when its gates will swing with no one in it, after they have remained in it for ahqab (ages)."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Hellfire is the swiftest of the two abodes to be populated and the swiftest to be ruined."

Ibn Jarir also related another opinion on this, saying: "Others said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, informed us of His will regarding the people of Paradise, so we understood the meaning of its exception through His saying ﴿a gift unbroken﴾. And it is in addition to the duration of the heavens and the earth. They said: He did not inform us of His will regarding the people of the Fire. It is permissible that His will refers to an increase, and it is permissible that it refers to a decrease."

Yunus narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd commented on the words of the Exalted: ﴿They shall abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿a gift unbroken﴾, and then said: "He informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, so He said ﴿a gift unbroken﴾, and He did not inform us of what He wills for the people of the Fire."

Ibn Mardawayh said in his tafsir: Sulayman ibn Ahmad narrated to us; Jubayr ibn 'Arfah narrated to us; Yazid ibn Marwan al-Khallal narrated to us; Abu Khalid narrated to us; Sufyan, meaning al-Thawri, narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿As for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire; for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If God wills to bring out some people from among those who were wretched from the Fire and admit them to Paradise, He will do so."

This hadith indicates that the exception applies only to bringing people out of the Fire after entering it, contrary to those who claim it refers to what precedes entry. It only indicates the removal of some of them from the Fire, and this is true beyond doubt, and it does not negate its ending, the extinction of its punishment, and its consuming those within it, and that they are tormented therein forever for as long as it remains so, ﴿and they shall not be removed from it﴾.

The hadith indicates two matters:
The first: that some of the wretched, if God wills, will be brought out of the Fire, which is the Fire of "He does" (fa'ala, i.e., the Fire that acts); and that the exception applies only to what comes after entering it, not what comes before.

Accordingly, the meaning of the exception is "except what your Lord wills" concerning the wretched, for they will not remain in it forever. The wretched will then be of two kinds: one kind will be brought out of the Fire, and another kind will remain in it forever. Thus they will be among "those who were wretched" first and then become among "those who were blessed," so that wretchedness and blessedness will both belong to them at two different times. They said: The Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, Hell has been a lying in wait, a place of return for the transgressors, abiding therein for ages. They will not taste therein any coolness or drink, except boiling water and dark, foul liquid, as a fitting recompense. Indeed, they used not to expect any reckoning, and they denied Our signs with complete denial﴾.

This is explicit in threatening the disbelievers who denied His signs, and it cannot be measured by these ahqab (ages) or by anything else, just as the eternal (qadim) cannot be measured by them. For this reason 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr said, as narrated by Shu'bah from Abu Balj, who heard 'Amr ibn Maymun narrate from him: "There will surely come upon Hellfire a day when its gates will clap with no one in it, and that will be after they have remained in it for ahqab."

(Section)
Those who affirmed the perpetuity of the Fire hold six lines of argument:

The first is the belief in consensus (ijma'). Many people believe this matter to be agreed upon among the Companions and the Followers, with no disagreement on it, and that disagreement about it arose later, and it is among the statements of the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah).

The second line: the Qur'an indicates this with definitive evidence. The Exalted informed that it is a lasting punishment (adhab muqim), that it does not slacken for them, that it will only increase their punishment, and that they will abide therein forever, ﴿and they will not come out of it﴾, meaning from the Fire, ﴿and they shall not be removed from it﴾. And that God has forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers, and that they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle, and that no decree will be passed upon them so that they die, and that its punishment will not be lightened for them, and that its punishment was "ghuram" (a constant, inescapable torment), meaning lasting and binding. They said: This indicates certainty of its perpetuity and continuity.

The third line: the widely transmitted Sunnah has informed that those in whose heart there is an atom's weight of faith will be brought out, but not the disbelievers. The hadiths of intercession, from beginning to end, are explicit that the sinful monotheists will come out of the Fire, and that this ruling is specific to them. So if the disbelievers were to come out, they would be in the same position as them, and the bringing out would not be specific to the people of faith.

The fourth line: the Messenger (ﷺ) informed us of this and we know it from his religion by necessity, without need for a specific transmission, just as we know from his religion the perpetuity of Paradise and that it does not perish.

The fifth line: the creeds of the early generations (salaf) and the People of the Sunnah explicitly state that Paradise and the Fire are created, and that they do not perish but are everlasting; and they only mention their perishing in reference to the people of innovation.

The sixth line: reason decides that the disbelievers abide in the Fire forever. This is based on a principle: whether the Return (ma'ad), the reward of obedient souls, and the punishment of wicked souls are known by reason or are known only through revelation (sam'). On this there are two approaches among the theologians (nuzzar) of the Muslims. Many of them hold that this is known by reason together with revelation, as the Qur'an indicates in many places, such as His denunciation of those who claim that He treats the righteous and the wicked alike in life and death, and of those who claim that He created His creation in vain and that they will not return to Him, and that He leaves them neglected, meaning He neither rewards nor punishes them; and that this impugns His wisdom and perfection and attributes to Him what is unfitting for Him. They often explain it by saying that human souls remain, and their beliefs and qualities cling to them and do not leave them; and even if they regret them when they see the punishment, they do not regret them because of their ugliness or because their Lord dislikes them, but rather, if the punishment were removed from them, they would return to what they were at first. The Exalted said: ﴿If only you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, "Oh, would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers." But rather there has appeared to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ These have tasted the punishment and experienced it, and its cause and its requirement have not ceased from their souls; rather their corruption and disbelief remain within them, not departing from them, such that if they were returned they would revert to disbelief as they were. This indicates that the perpetuity of their punishment is decreed by reason as it is brought by revelation.

Those who hold the perishing of the Fire said: The discussion of these lines clarifies the correct position on this question.

As for the first line: the consensus you claim is not established. Only someone who is unaware of the dispute imagines a consensus on this matter, but the dispute over it has been known from early times until now. Indeed, if the one claiming consensus were required to transmit from ten Companions or fewer down to one that he said the Fire will never perish, he would find no way to do so. We, however, have transmitted from them explicit statements to the contrary; we have not found from any one of them a statement otherwise. Rather, the Followers related both this and that from them. They said: The consensus that is valid is of two kinds, agreed upon, and a third kind that is disputed; and none of these exist on this question. The first kind is what is known as a necessary part of the religion (ma'lum min darurat al-din), such as the obligation of the pillars of Islam and the prohibition of the manifest prohibitions. The second is what is transmitted from the scholars of ijtihad (independent reasoning) explicitly stating its ruling. The third is that some say an opinion and it spreads among the community and no one rejects it. So where, among you, is one of these types? And if someone claimed consensus by these means, arguing that the Companions were reported to have held it and no one among them objected to him, he would be more entitled to the claim of consensus than you. They said: As for the second line, namely the Qur'an's indication of the Fire's continuance and non-perishing, where in the Qur'an is a single proof indicating that?

Indeed, what the Qur'an indicates is that the disbelievers abide in the Fire forever, that they will not be removed from it, that its punishment will not slacken for them, that they will not die therein, that their punishment therein is lasting, and that it is a binding ghuram for them. All of this is not disputed among the Companions, the Followers, and the Imams of the Muslims, and this is not the point of contention. The dispute lies in another matter: whether the Fire is everlasting (abadiyyah) or is among what God has decreed shall perish.

As for the disbelievers not being removed from it, that its punishment will not slacken for them, that no decree will be passed upon them so that they die, and that they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle, no one among the Companions, the Followers, or the People of the Sunnah has disagreed about this. Only those whose statements we have related, from among the Jews, the Ittihadiyyah (those who claim unity of existence), and some people of innovation, have disagreed on this. These texts and their like require that they abide forever in the abode of punishment as long as it remains, and that they never come out of it while it endures, just as the People of Monotheism come out of it while it endures. The difference is between one who is released from a prison that remains in its state, and one whose imprisonment is nullified by the prison's ruin and collapse.

They said: As for the third line, namely the arrival of the Sunnah widely transmitted that the people of major sins will come out of the Fire while the people of polytheism will not, it is true beyond doubt; and it only indicates what we have said: that the monotheists come out of it while it is an abode of punishment that has not perished, and the polytheists remain in it as long as it endures. The texts indicate this, and in this sense they said.

As for the fourth line, namely that the Messenger (ﷺ) informed us of this by necessity: there is no doubt that it is known by necessity from his religion that the disbelievers remain in it as long as it endures. This is known from his religion by necessity. But as for its being everlasting, without end and never perishing like Paradise, where in the Qur'an or the Sunnah is a single proof that indicates that?

They said: As for the fifth line, namely that the creed of the People of the Sunnah holds that Paradise and the Fire are created and will never perish, there is no doubt that the claim of their perishing is the view of the people of innovation, the Jahmiyyah and the Mu'tazilah. And this view was not held by any of the Companions, the Followers, or any of the Imams of the Muslims. As for the perishing of the Fire alone, we have shown you those among the Companions who held it, and their distinction between Paradise and the Fire. How then can the view be among the views of the people of innovation, when it is not known that anyone among the people of innovation distinguished between the two abodes? Your claim that it is among the views of the people of innovation is the statement of one who has no knowledge of the doctrines and opinions and disagreements of the children of Adam.

They said: The view that is counted among the views of the people of innovation is what contradicts the Book of God, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the consensus of the community, whether of the Companions or those after them; or a view that agrees with the Book and the Sunnah. The statements of the Companions are not counted among the views of the people of innovation, even if they adopted and believed them. The truth must be accepted from whoever says it, and falsehood must be rejected from whoever says it.

Mu'adh ibn Jabal used to say: "God is the Judge, the Just. The doubters are destroyed. Indeed, behind you are trials in which wealth will abound, and the Qur'an will be made accessible, so that the believer, the hypocrite, the woman, the child, the black and the red will read it, and one of them will soon say, 'I have read the Qur'an, so I do not think they will follow me until I invent something else for them.' So beware of innovation, for every innovation is misguidance. And beware of the deviation of the wise, for Satan may speak through the tongue of the wise with a word of misguidance, and the hypocrite may speak a word of truth. So accept the truth from whoever brings it, for truth has a light." They asked: "What is the deviation of the wise?" He said: "It is a word that startles you and that you reject, and you say, 'What is this?' So beware of his deviation and do not let it turn you away from him, for he will soon return and retract, and knowledge and faith have their place until the Day of Resurrection."

What the People of the Sunnah reported in their creeds is what the Book and the Sunnah indicate, and what the early generations agreed upon: that Paradise and the Fire are created, that the people of the Fire will not come out of it, that its punishment will not be lightened for them nor slacken, that they abide therein forever, and whoever among them said that the Fire will never perish forever only said so because he thought some people of innovation held its perishing, and the narrations mentioned above did not reach him.

They said: As for the rational judgment that the people of the Fire abide in it forever, it is an assertion about reason of what is not in its domain, for this question is among those matters that can only be known through the report of the truthful one. As for the principle of reward and punishment, whether it is known by reason together with revelation, or only by revelation alone, there are two views among the theologians of the Muslims, from the followers of the four Imams and others. The correct view is that reason indicates the Return, the reward, and the punishment in general terms; but its details can only be known through revelation, and the perpetuity of reward and punishment is not indicated by reason alone, but is known only through revelation. Revelation has indicated with definitive evidence the perpetuity of the reward of the obedient. As for the punishment of the disobedient, revelation has also indicated with definitive evidence its ending for the monotheists. As for its perpetuity or ending for the disbelievers, this is the field of contention. Whoever has revelation on his side is more entitled to the correct view. And success is from God.

Section: We will mention the difference between the perpetuity of Paradise and of the Fire, legally and rationally. This becomes clear in several respects:

The first: God, glory be to Him, informed of the lasting bliss of the people of Paradise, that it has no exhaustion and no cessation, and that it is "unbroken" (ghayr majdhudh). As for the Fire, He did not inform us of more than that its people abide therein, do not leave it, do not die therein nor live, that it is closed over them, that whenever they wish to leave it they are returned therein, that its punishment is binding upon them, and that it remains over them and does not slacken for them. The difference between the two reports is clear.

The second: In three verses, God, glory be to Him, has informed about the Fire in a way that indicates it is not everlasting. The first is His saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as God wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing.﴾ The second is His saying: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is the Executor of what He wills.﴾ The third is His saying: ﴿abiding therein for ages.﴾ Had it not been for the definitive proofs indicating the everlastingness and perpetuity of Paradise, the ruling on the two exceptions in the two places would have been one. How, when the two verses contain context that distinguishes between the two exceptions? For He said regarding the people of the Fire: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Executor of what He wills﴾, so we know that God wills to do an act He has not told us about. And He said regarding the people of Paradise: "a gift unbroken," so we know that this gift and bliss are not cut off from them ever. The punishment is timed and conditional, while the bliss is neither timed nor conditional.

The third: It is established that no one who never did any good enters Paradise among those punished whom God brings out of the Fire; but as for the Fire, no one enters it who never did any evil, and no one is punished except one who disobeyed Him.

The fourth: It is established that God, glory be to Him, creates a new creation for Paradise on the Day of Resurrection to dwell in it, and He does not do that for the Fire.

As for the hadith related in Sahih al-Bukhari: "As for the Fire, God will create for it other people," it is an error made by some narrators, in which the wording of the hadith was reversed for him. The actual text is what al-Bukhari cited in the same chapter: "As for Paradise, God will create for it other people." Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, mentioned this to show that the wording was reversed for the one who narrated it contrary to this and that. The point is that the Fire may not be measured against Paradise in terms of eternity given these differences.

The fifth respect clarifies this: Paradise is from the requirement of His mercy and pleasure, while the Fire is from His wrath and displeasure. His mercy overcomes His wrath and precedes it, as is established in the authentic hadith from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When God had decreed creation, He wrote in a book that is placed with Him upon the Throne: 'My mercy overcomes My wrath.'" If His pleasure precedes His wrath and overcomes it, then equating what results from His pleasure with what results from His wrath is impossible.

The sixth respect clarifies this: what is by mercy and for mercy is intended for its own sake, the intended end; whereas what is from the requirement of wrath and displeasure is intended for something else, as a means. The latter is preceded and overcome, desired for something other than itself. What is by mercy is victorious, precedent, and desired for its own sake.

The seventh respect clarifies this: God, glory be to Him, said to Paradise: "You are My mercy; I show mercy through you to whom I will." And He said to the Fire: "You are My punishment; I punish through you whom I will." His punishment is a separate act, arising from His wrath, while His mercy here is Paradise, a created mercy arising from the mercy that is an attribute of the Most Merciful. Thus there are four matters here: a mercy that is His attribute; a separate reward arising from His mercy; a wrath that subsists in Him, the Glorified; and a separate punishment arising from it. When the attribute of mercy overcomes the attribute of wrath, then what is by mercy overcoming what is by wrath is all the more fitting and proper. Thus the Fire that arose from wrath cannot withstand Paradise that arose from mercy.

This is clarified by the eighth aspect: Hell was created as a warning to the believers and a purification for the sinners and the wrongdoers. It is a cleansing from the impurity that the soul acquired in this world. If a person purifies himself here through sincere repentance, good deeds that erase sins, and afflictions that expiate them, he will not need to be purified there. It is said to him, together with the company of the good: ﴿Peace be upon you. You are good, so enter it, abiding forever.﴾ But if he was not purified in this abode and arrives in the Hereafter with his filth, his impurity and his defilement, he is admitted into the Fire as a purification for him. His stay in the Fire is in proportion to the removal of that filth, impurity and uncleanness which water cannot wash away. When he is perfectly purified, he is brought out of the Fire.

God, glory be to Him, created His servants upright in monotheism (hanif), and this is the fitrah (innate disposition) of God upon which He created mankind. If they were left alone with their fitrah, they would grow up only upon monotheism. But something came upon the majority of people that changed it, and this is why the share of the Fire is greater than the share of Paradise. This alteration has degrees that none can count except God. So God sent His messengers and revealed His books, reminding His servants of the fitrah upon which He created them. Those who were granted success, for whom the good reward from God had been decreed, recognized through the original fitrah the truth of what the messengers brought and the books revealed. Thus the law of God and His religion, which He sent with His messengers, agreed with their fitrah. The revealed law and the perfected fitrah protected them from their souls acquiring impurity, uncleanness and filth that would cling to them and not leave them. Rather, whenever some of that touched them, and a visitation from Satan afflicted them, they attacked it with the law and the fitrah and removed its effect and its trace. The Lord, exalted is He, perfected this for them through decrees He ordains for them, whether they love or dislike them, which purge from them those traces that had disturbed the fitrah. Then the demand of mercy came and found a receptive place, prepared for it, with nothing to repel it. So it said: "Here I am commanded." God, glory be to Him, has no purpose in tormenting His servants without a cause, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And God is ever Appreciative and Knowing.﴾

The wretched continued with the alteration of the fitrah and its transformation from what it was created upon to its opposite, until corruption became firmly established and the alteration was complete. Then they needed, to remove this, another alteration and a purification that would return them to health, since the signs of God, recited and created, and His decrees, loved and disliked, in this abode did not return them. So He provided for them other signs, decrees and punishments beyond what they had in this world, to extract that filth and uncleanness which cannot be removed except by the Fire. When the cause and reason for the punishment is removed, the punishment is removed, and the demand of mercy remains with no opposition.

If it is said: "This is true, but the cause of punishment is only removed when the cause is accidental, like the sins of the monotheists. As for when it is inherent, like disbelief and polytheism, its effect does not go away, just as the cause does not go away." God, glory be to Him, has indicated this very meaning in several places in His Book, among them His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden.﴾ This is information that their souls and natures demand nothing but disbelief and polytheism, and that they are not receptive to faith at all. Among them is His saying: ﴿And whoever was blind in this [life] will be blind in the Hereafter and more astray in way.﴾ So He, glory be to Him, informed that their misguidance and blindness to guidance are lasting and do not cease, even with direct observation of the realities that the messengers told them about. And if blindness and misguidance do not leave them, then their effect, their consequence and their requirement do not leave them either. Among them is His saying: ﴿And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while being refusers.﴾ This indicates that there is no good in them that would call for mercy, and if there were any good in them He would not have wasted its effect upon them. It also indicates that there is no good in them even there, in His saying: "Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart an atom's weight of good." So if these people had even the least atom's weight of good, they would have come out with those who came out.

It is said: "By the Lord's life, this is among the strongest things to rely upon on this question, and the matter is as you say: punishment lasts as long as its cause and reason last. There is no doubt that in the Hereafter they are in blindness and misguidance as they were in this world, and their inner selves are corrupt as they were in this world. The punishment continues upon them and remains as long as they are in that state. But is this disbelief, denial and corruption something intrinsic to them, whose removal is impossible, or is it an accidental, incidental matter upon the fitrah that is capable of being removed? This is the crux of the question. You have nothing in hand that shows its removal is impossible or that it is intrinsic." God, glory be to Him, has informed that He created His servants upon the upright monotheism (hanifiyyah) and that the devils led them astray from it. He did not create them upon disbelief and denial, as He created a beast upon its nature. Rather, He created them upon acknowledging their Creator, loving Him and affirming His oneness. If this truth upon which they were created and originated can be removed by disbelief and false polytheism, then the removal of disbelief and false polytheism by its opposite, the truth, is more fitting and more worthy. There is no doubt that if they were returned to the state they are in, they would return to what they were forbidden. But from where do you know that this state will not be removed or changed by another creation, which the Blessed and Exalted One will bring them into when the Fire has taken its effect upon them and the desired wisdom of their punishment has been achieved? For punishment was not aimless; it was for a desired wisdom. When that wisdom is achieved, nothing remains in the punishment that is required and no purpose remains to be intended. God, glory be to Him, does not take pleasure in the punishment of His servants as an oppressed person takes his satisfaction from his oppressor. He does not punish His servant for this purpose. Rather, He punishes him for his purification and out of mercy for him. So His punishment is a benefit to him, even if he suffers from it the utmost pain, just as His punishment by legal penalties (hudud) in this world is a benefit to those upon whom they are carried out."

God, glory be to Him, has called the legal penalty a punishment ('adhab). His wisdom has decreed that He made for every disease a remedy suitable to it. The remedy for the one who has gone astray is among the most painful remedies. The compassionate physician applies cauterization to the patient with fire, again and again, to extract from him the corrupt matter that arose upon an upright nature. And if he sees that amputating a limb is better for the sick person, he amputates it and makes him taste the greatest pain. This is the decree and destiny of the Lord in removing a foreign matter that came upon an upright nature without the servant's choice. How much more so when corrupt matters come upon a sound fitrah by the servant's own choice and will. Whoever of the intelligent reflects upon the law of God, the Blessed and Exalted One, and His decree in this world, and His reward and punishment in the Hereafter, will find that they are in the utmost harmony and agreement, and that they are bound to one another. For the source of all of them is complete knowledge, perfect wisdom and encompassing mercy. He, glory be to Him, is the Manifest True King, and His kingship is a kingship of mercy, benevolence and justice.

The ninth aspect: His punishment of the servant is not because He needs to punish him, nor for a benefit that returns to Him, nor to repel a harm or a pain that is removed from Him by the punishment. Rather, He is exalted above that and free of it, as He is exalted above all defects and deficiencies. Nor is it pure vanity devoid of wisdom and praiseworthy aim, for He is also free of that and exalted above it. Rather, it is either part of the completion of the bliss of His friends and beloved ones, or it is for the benefit and treatment of the wretched, or it is for both. In all three possibilities, punishment is a matter intended for something else, the intention of means rather than the intention of ends. The point is that when the means achieves the desired result, its ruling ceases. The bliss of His friends does not depend, in its origin or its perfection, on the continuation of the punishment of His enemies or its perpetuity. The benefit of the wretched does not lie in its perpetuity and continuation, even though there is a benefit for them in the very origin of punishment.

The tenth aspect: the pleasure (rida) and mercy of the Lord, blessed and exalted, are two essential attributes of His. There is no end to His pleasure. Rather, as the one most knowledgeable of Him among creation said: "Glory be to God and praise Him, as many as His creation, and as much as the pleasure of Himself, and as much as the weight of His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words." So if His mercy has overcome His wrath, then the pleasure of His Self is higher and greater. For His good pleasure is greater than the Gardens and their bliss and everything in them. He has informed the people of Paradise that His good pleasure descends upon them, so He is never displeased with them again. As for His wrath and anger, blessed and exalted is He, they are not among His essential attributes, which cannot be separated from Him, such that He has always been and always will be angry. The people have two opinions regarding the attribute of anger. One is that it is among His active attributes subsisting in Him, like all His actions. The other is that it is an attribute of action separate from Him, not subsisting in Him. In either case, it is not like life, knowledge and power, which are impossible for Him to be separated from. Punishment arises only from the attribute of His anger, and the Fire was kindled only by His anger. It has been reported in a raised (marfu') narration that God created a creation from His anger and settled them in the east, and He takes vengeance through them upon whoever disobeys Him. So His creations are of two kinds: a kind created from mercy and by mercy, and a kind created from anger and by anger. For He, glory be to Him, possesses absolute perfection in every respect, which is exempt from the assumption of its opposite. Among these attributes: He is pleased and angered, rewards and punishes, gives and withholds, honors and humiliates, takes vengeance and pardons. Indeed, this is the requirement of His true kingship, and the reality of a kingship joined with wisdom, mercy and praise. When His anger, glory be to Him and exalted is He, is removed and replaced by His pleasure, His punishment is removed and replaced by His mercy, and the punishment turns into mercy. Indeed, it was never anything but mercy, even if its kind and form differ, just as the punishment of the disobedient was mercy, and bringing them out of the Fire is mercy. They turned in His mercy in this world, and they turn in it in the Hereafter. But that mercy they love and it agrees with their natures, while this mercy they dislike and it is hard upon them, like the mercy of the physician who cuts the flesh of the patient and applies cauterizing irons to extract from him the corrupt, rotten matters.

If it is said: "This comparison is not valid, for the physician does this to the patient while the patient loves him and is pleased with him, and his action does not arise from anger, nor from his being angry with the patient. This is why it is not called punishment. But the punishment of these people came about only by God's anger upon them, and it is pure punishment." It is answered: "This is true, but it does not contradict its being a mercy to them, even though it is a punishment for them. This is like the carrying out of legal penalties upon them in this world, which is punishment, mercy, lightening and purification. The legal penalties are a purification for those upon whom they are carried out, and a punishment. They provoked the Lord, exalted is He, and confronted Him with what is not fitting to confront Him with, dealt with Him in the worst manner, denied Him and denied His messengers, made the least of His creatures and the most wicked and most hateful of them equal to Him, associated with Him other gods, preferred their own pleasure over His pleasure and their obedience over His obedience. He is the one who bestowed favors upon them: He is their Creator, their Provider and their true Master. So His hatred of them became intense and His anger upon them grew. That requires the perfection of His names and attributes, whose opposite it is impossible to suppose of Him, and it is impossible that the effects and requirements of those attributes be separated from Him. Rather, to suspend their rulings would be a nullification of them, just as to deny them would be a nullification of their realities. Both nullifications are impossible for Him, glory be to Him and exalted is He. The nullifiers are of two kinds: one nullifies His attributes, and the other nullifies their rulings and their requirements. This punishment was a punishment upon them from this aspect, and a remedy for them from the aspect of the mercy that precedes the anger. So both matters are combined in it. When the anger is removed by the removal of the corrupt matter, through the change of the nature that required it in the Hellfire, after the passing of ages upon it, and the wisdom that required the punishment is achieved, mercy does its work and seeks its effect, with no opposition." This is clarified by:

The eleventh aspect: pardon is more beloved to Him, glory be to Him, than retribution; mercy is more beloved to Him than punishment; pleasure is more beloved to Him than anger; and grace is more beloved to Him than justice. For this reason, the effects of this love appear in His law and His decree, and they become most manifest to His servants in His reward and His punishment. Since this is the more beloved of the two matters to Him, and for it He created creation, revealed the books and legislated the laws, and His power is suitable for everything, lacking in no respect, and those corrupt, foul matters are a disease among the diseases, while in His hand, glory be to Him and exalted is He, lies the complete cure and the remedies suited to every ailment, and He possesses complete power, encompassing mercy and absolute self-sufficiency, then the servant is in greater need of one who treats his illness, which has reached the extreme of harm and hardship. The servant knows that he is ill, and that his remedy is in the hand of the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. So he humbles himself before Him, enters upon Him through it, submits to Him, his heart breaks before Him, he is humbled before His might, and he knows that all praise is His, all truth is His, that He is the Unjust, the Ignorant (the one who attributes injustice and ignorance to himself), and that his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, deals with him by His full justice, not by a part of His justice. He knows that to Him belongs the ultimate praise for what He has done to him, that His praise is what placed him in this station and brought him to Him, and that he has no good in himself in any respect; rather, that is pure grace from God and His charity upon him. He knows that there is no deliverance for him from what he is in except by mere pardon and overlooking of his right. So his self deserves every blame, defect and deficiency, and his Lord, exalted is He, deserves every praise, perfection and commendation. If the people of Hell were to witness His bounty, glory be to Him, His mercy, His perfection and His praise, which has made all of that obligatory for them, and they sought His good pleasure, even by remaining in that state, and said: "If what we are in is Your pleasure, then Your pleasure is what we want. We did not reach this state except by seeking what does not please You. But if this pleases You from us, then Your pleasure is the utmost of what we aim for, and no pain of a wound is painful when You are pleased. You are more merciful to us than ourselves and more knowledgeable of our interests. To You belongs all praise; whether You punish or pardon, You are praised," the Fire would become cool and peace for them.

Imam Ahmad has narrated in his Musnad, from the hadith of al-Aswad ibn Sari', that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Four will come on the Day of Resurrection: a deaf man who hears nothing, a fool, an elderly man senile with age, and a man who died in a period of no messengers (fatrah). As for the deaf man, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come, and I hear nothing.' As for the fool, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come, and the children were pelting me with dung.' As for the senile man, he will say: 'My Lord, Islam has come, and I understand nothing.' As for the one who died in the fatrah, he will say: 'My Lord, no messenger came to me from You.' So He will take their covenants that they will obey Him, and He will send to them: 'Enter the Fire.'" He said: "By the One in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, if they had entered it, it would have been cool and peace for them." In the Musnad also, from the hadith of Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, a similar report, and it says: "Whoever enters it, it will be cool and peace for him, and whoever does not enter it will be dragged into it." So these people, because they were pleased with their punishment and hastened to it, knowing that in it was the good pleasure of their Lord and conformity with His command and love, it turned into bliss for them.

A similar report is what Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated: Rushdin told me, from Ibn An'um, from Abu Uthman, that he told him, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Two men among those who enter the Fire are screaming loudly. The Lord, majestic is His majesty, says: 'Bring them out.' When they are brought out, He says to them: 'Why were you screaming loudly?'
They say: 'We did that so that You would have mercy on us.'
He says: 'My mercy upon you is that you go and throw yourselves wherever you were in the Fire.'
So they go, and one of them throws himself, and God makes it cool and peace for him. The other stands and does not throw himself. The Lord, blessed and exalted, says to him: 'What prevented you from throwing yourself as your companion threw himself?'
He says: 'My Lord, I hope You will not return me to it after You have brought me out of it.'
The Lord, blessed and exalted, says: 'You will have what you hoped for.' So both enter Paradise together by the mercy of God."

Al-Awza'i mentioned, from Bilal ibn Sa'd, who said: "It will be ordered that two men be brought out of the Fire. When they come out and stand, God says to them: 'How did you find your resting place and the evil of your end?' They say: 'The worst resting place and the worst end that a servant has come to.' He says to them: 'Because of what your hands have sent forward. And I am not unjust to the servants.'
He said: Then it is ordered that they be returned to the Fire. As for one of them, he goes in his shackles and chains until he plunges into it. As for the other, he hesitates, so it is ordered that both be returned. He says to the one who went in his shackles and chains until he plunged into it: 'What moved you to do what you did, when you had come out of it?' He says: 'I learned of the consequence of Your disobedience, and I did not want to expose myself to Your wrath a second time.' He says to the one who hesitated: 'What moved you to do what you did?' He says: 'My good opinion of You, when You brought me out of it, that You would not return me to it.' So He has mercy on both of them and orders them to Paradise."

The twelfth aspect: bounty and reward follow from His mercy, forgiveness, kindness and generosity. For this reason He attributes them to Himself. Punishment and retribution, however, come from His creatures, so He is not named "the Punisher" or "the Tormentor." He distinguishes between them, making the former one of His attributes and the latter one of His acts, even within a single verse, as in His saying: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾. He also said: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in retribution, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and a similar verse is at the end of al-An'am. Whatever is required by His names and attributes endures with their endurance, especially when it is beloved to Him, and it is an end sought in itself. As for evil, which is punishment, it does not belong to His names and attributes. It enters His acts only for a wisdom which, once achieved, ceases and passes away. By contrast, He, glorified and exalted, is perpetually the Giver of benefit; His benefit never ceases, and His kindness is eternal and everlasting. Thus He has always been and always will be the Punisher, perpetually angry, perpetually avenging. Reflect carefully on this aspect, for in matters of Allah's names and attributes it opens for you a door of knowing Him and loving Him, and it clarifies this.

The thirteenth aspect: this is the saying of the one most knowledgeable of His creation about Him, and the most aware of His names and attributes: "Evil is not attributed to You." Whoever said "evil is not drawn near to You" did not grasp the intended meaning. Rather, evil is never attributed to Him, glorified be He, in any respect: not in His essence, not in His attributes, not in His acts, and not in His names. His essence possesses absolute perfection in every respect; all His attributes are attributes of perfection, He is praised for them and extolled by them; His acts are all good, mercy, justice and wisdom, with no evil in them in any way; and His names are all most beautiful. How, then, could evil be attributed to Him? Evil lies rather in His acted-upon creations, which are separate from Him, since His act is not something acted upon. His act is wholly good, whereas the created, acted-upon thing contains both good and evil. When evil is a created thing separate from the Lord, glorified be He, and not subsisting in Him, it is not attributed to Him. He did not say "You do not create evil," so that his statement would need interpretation; rather, he denied that evil is attributed to Him in attribute, in act, and in name. Once this is understood, evil is nothing but sins and their consequences, while the opposite is faith and acts of obedience and their consequences. Faith and acts of obedience are connected to Him, glorified be He, and for their sake Allah created His creation, sent His messengers, and revealed His books. They are praise of the Lord, blessed and exalted, and honour, magnification, and worship of Him. These have effects that they seek and require, so their effects endure with the endurance of their object. As for evils, they are not sought for their own sake, nor are they the ultimate purpose for which creation was made. They are acted-upon things decreed for a beloved matter and made a means to it. When what they were decreed for is achieved, they vanish and dissolve, and the matter returns to pure good.

The fourteenth aspect: He, glorified and exalted, has informed us that His mercy encompasses everything, so there is nothing among things except that it contains His mercy. This is not contradicted by the fact that you show mercy to a servant through something that distresses and pains him and that he intensely dislikes, for that too is part of mercy, as has already been explained. We have already mentioned the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) above, and His saying, exalted be He, to the two men: "My mercy for you both, if you set out and go to your souls wherever you are, from the Fire." It has also come in some reports that when a servant prays for one who has been afflicted with severe trial and says, "O Allah, have mercy on him," the Lord, blessed and exalted, says: "How can I have mercy on him through the very thing by which I have mercy on him?" Thus trial is a mercy from Him to His servants. In a divine report, Allah, exalted be He, says: "Those who remember Me are the people of My sitting, those who obey Me are the people of My honour, those who thank Me are the people of My increase, and those who disobey Me—I shall make them despair of My mercy, and if they repent, then I am their beloved, and if they do not repent, then I am their physician. I test them with calamities to purify them from their faults." So trial and punishment are decreed by Him to remove diseases that cannot be removed except by them, and the Fire is the greatest remedy. Whoever is treated in this world, that will spare him the remedy in the Hereafter; otherwise he must have a remedy according to his disease. Whoever knows the Lord, blessed and exalted, through the attributes of His majesty and the descriptions of His perfection, through His wisdom, mercy, goodness, kindness, self-sufficiency, generosity, His love for His servants, His desire to bestow favour upon them, and the precedence of His mercy towards them, will hasten not to deny this, if he does not hasten to accept it.

This is clarified by the fifteenth aspect: His acts never depart from wisdom, mercy, benefit, and justice. He does not act in vain, nor unjustly, nor falsely, but He is exalted above all that, just as He is exalted above all defects and deficiencies. Once this is established, their punishment, if it is mercy towards them so that that impurity is removed and purity is completed, is evident. If it is for a wisdom, then once that sought wisdom is achieved, the punishment ceases, and wisdom does not require the eternal perpetuity of punishment in which it would be perpetual with the perpetuity of the Lord, blessed and exalted. If it is for a benefit: if that benefit returns to them, then their benefit does not lie in their remaining in punishment in this way; and if the benefit returns to His friends, then that is more perfect for their bliss, and this does not require the perpetuity of punishment. The bliss of His friends and its perfection do not depend on their fathers, sons and spouses remaining in everlasting punishment. If you say that this is what mercy, wisdom and benefit require, you have said what is unintelligible. If you say that it is due to pure will, with no wisdom or end sought in it, then the answer is in two respects. First, that it is impossible for the Most Wise of judges and the Most Knowing of the worlds that His acts should be void of wisdom, benefits, and praiseworthy ends; the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the proofs of reason and nature, and the visible signs bear witness to the falsity of this. Second, if the matter were so, then their remaining in punishment and its cessation would be equal in relation to His will, and its ending would not conflict with His perfection. He, glorified be He, has not informed us that the punishment is everlasting and without end. In this case the best that can be said is that it is among the possible things, whose judgment depends on the report of the Truthful. If one follows the path of explaining by wisdom, mercy and benefit, it does not require perpetuity; and if one follows the path of pure will that is not explained by reasons, it does not require it either. And if the matter rests on mere reports, there is no text which requires it.

The sixteenth aspect: His mercy, glorified be He, precedes His wrath towards those who are punished. He created them by His mercy, nurtured them by His mercy, provided for them and granted them well-being by His mercy, and sent messengers to them by His mercy. The causes of vengeance and punishment come after the causes of mercy and are incidental to them. So His mercy precedes His wrath towards them, and He created them in a form in which His mercy towards them is nearer than His wrath and punishment. For this reason you see that the mercy of the Lord has encompassed the children of unbelievers, so whoever sees them feels mercy for them; and for this reason He forbade their killing. His mercy precedes His wrath towards them, so it is what comes first to them. In every state they are within His mercy, both in their well-being and in their trial.

When mercy is what precedes in them, its effect is not wholly nullified even if the effect of wrath and displeasure opposes it, and that is due to a cause on their part. The effect of mercy, however, has its cause from Him, glorified and exalted. What comes from Him requires their mercy, and what comes from them requires their punishment. What comes from Him is prior and dominant. If His mercy overcomes His wrath, then the effect of mercy overcoming the effect of wrath is all the more fitting and more appropriate.

The seventeenth aspect: He, glorified and exalted, describes punishment as "the punishment of a barren day," "the punishment of a great day," and "the punishment of a painful day," but He does not describe bliss as "the bliss of a day," neither in this place nor in any other. It is established in the authentic collections that the Day of Resurrection is measured as fifty thousand years. The damned differ in the length of their stay in punishment according to their crimes. Allah, glorified be He, made the punishment according to what was in this world and its causes, and according to what was intended by the worldly and what was not intended for Allah. So the punishment is in accordance with that. As for what was intended for the Hereafter and was intended for the Face of Allah, there is no punishment for it. The world has a term set for it at which it ends. Whatever passes from it to that abode that is not for Allah is what is punished by it. As for what was intended for the Face of Allah and the Hereafter, it was intended for what does not perish and does not cease, so it endures with the endurance of what it is intended for. For when the sought end is lasting and does not cease, what is attached to it does not cease so long as it does not cease. This is unlike a perishing and passing end. Whatever is intended other than Allah perishes and ceases with the cessation of its object and its aim. What is intended for the Face of Allah remains with the remaining of the sought object. So when the world perishes, its causes are cut off, and the deeds and beings that were in it for other than Allah are transferred and turned into punishment and pains, they have no object to which they are attached that endures with its endurance. This is unlike bliss.

The eighteenth aspect: It is not within the wisdom of the Most Wise of judges that He create a creation and punish them forever, in an everlasting punishment without end and without cessation. The textual, rational and innate proofs show that He, glorified and exalted, is Wise and is the Most Wise of judges. So when He punishes His creation, He punishes them with wisdom, just as punishment and retribution occur in this world under His law and decree. For in it there are wisdoms and benefits: the purification and cure of the servant, the expulsion of harmful matter from him through those pains. The sound intellects witness this. In it there is also the purification and goodness of souls, their restraint, the deterrence of their likes, their being made to stop at their poverty and their need for their Lord, and other praiseworthy wisdoms and ends that none knows but Allah. There is no doubt that Paradise is good and that none enters it except the good. For this reason, when they have crossed the Bridge, they are held to account on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, where retribution is taken for some of them from others for wrongs that existed between them in the world. When they have been cleansed and purified, they are given permission to enter Paradise. It is known that wicked, corrupt and dark souls, which if returned to the world before punishment would return to what they were forbidden, are not fit to dwell in the Abode of Peace in the neighbourhood of the Lord of the worlds. So when they are punished in the Fire with a punishment by which their souls are freed from that corruption, filth and dirt, this is from the wisdom and mercy of the Most Wise of judges. The wisdom of creating souls in which there is evil that is removed by long trial and by the Fire does not conflict with wisdom, just as the impurities of gold, silver and iron are removed by fire. This is intelligible in wisdom and is among the requirements of a world created in this way. But creating souls whose evil never ceases and whose punishment has no end does not appear in wisdom and mercy. There is dispute among the intelligent about the existence of this type, namely beings that are evil in every respect and contain nothing good at all. Even if it were to exist, the Lord, blessed and exalted, is able to transform essences and change them and their attributes. So when the wisdom sought in creating these souls and the wisdom sought in punishing them are achieved, Allah, glorified be He, is able to bring them into existence in another form different from that form, and to show them in the second form another kind of mercy.

This is clarified by the nineteenth aspect: it is established that Allah, glorified and exalted, creates for Paradise another creation whom He causes to dwell in it, although they have never done any good, so that Paradise is a reward for them for it. When punishment has taken its course with these souls and the penalty has reached its limit, those souls are broken, humbled, abased, and acknowledge to their Lord and Creator praise, and that He is just towards them in every respect, and that in this state they are being lightened by Him. Had He willed that their punishment be harsher than that, He would have done it, and He willed that the penalty be written, seeking to accord with His pleasure and love, and knowing that punishment was more fitting for them and that nothing else befits them or suits them except Him. Thus all those corruptions melted from them and dissolved and were replaced by humility, brokenness, praise and glorification of the Lord, blessed and exalted. It was not within His wisdom that they continue in punishment after that, since their evil has been exchanged for good, their polytheism for monotheism, their arrogance for submission and humility. This is not contradicted by the words of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿If they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾. For that statement was made before the punishment that removes those corruptions had reached them. It was at the time of confrontation, before entering. He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." But it has become clear to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden; and indeed they are liars﴾. They said this before the punishment extracted from them those corruptions. But when they have remained in punishment for ages, and the ḥuqb (age), as al-Ṭabarānī narrated in his Muʿjam from the hadith of Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The ḥuqb is fifty thousand years," then it is far-fetched that arrogance, polytheism and corruption should remain after these lengthy periods in punishment.

The twentieth aspect: It is established in the two Sahihs, in the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri concerning the intercession, that He, mighty and majestic, says: "The angels have interceded, the Prophet (ﷺ) has interceded, and the believers have interceded, and there remains none but the Most Merciful of the merciful." He grasps a handful from the Fire and brings out a people who have never done any good; they have become charcoal, and He casts them into a river at the mouths of Paradise called the River of Life, and they come out as a seed comes out in the flood-borne debris. Allah says: "Paradise! These are the freed ones of Allah, whom Allah has admitted into Paradise without any deed they performed or any good they sent forward." These people had been burnt by the Fire entirely, so that there was no part of their bodies untouched by it, to the point that they became ḥumam, which is charcoal burnt by fire. The apparent context indicates that there was not in their hearts even an atom's weight of good, for the wording of the hadith is: "Then He says: Go back; whomever you find with an atom's weight of good in his heart, bring him out." So they bring out a great multitude. Then they say: "Our Lord, we have left none of good therein." Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "The angels have interceded, the Prophet (ﷺ) has interceded, and the believers have interceded, and there remains none but the Most Merciful of the merciful." Then Allah grasps a handful from the Fire and brings out a people who have never done any good. This context shows that these people did not have an atom's weight of good in their hearts, and yet mercy brought them out. Of this kind is the mercy of the Glorified and Exalted towards the man who instructed his family to burn him with fire and scatter his ashes on land and sea, supposing that he could escape Allah, glorified and exalted. This man doubted resurrection and the power of God, and had never done any good, yet when Allah asked him, "What moved you to do what you did?", he said, "Fear of You, and You know." So Allah had mercy on him and forgave him. For Allah, glorified and exalted, has in His creation wisdoms beyond the grasp of human intellects. It has been established in a hadith from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, mighty and majestic, says: Bring out from the Fire whoever remembered Me for a day or feared Me in a station." They said: "Who is it, in all his life from beginning to end, who never remembered Him for a single day nor feared Him for a single hour?" There is no doubt that when the mercy of the Glorified and Exalted brings out of the Fire whoever remembered Him for a time or feared Him in some station, it is no marvel that the Fire should be annulled; yet these came out of it while it was still a Fire.

The twenty-first aspect: when the servant truly confesses his sin, the confession includes attributing evil, wrongdoing and blame to himself in every respect, and attributing to his Lord, blessed and exalted, justice, praise, mercy and absolute perfection in every respect. He thereby seeks the tenderness of his Lord and asks for His mercy. When Allah wills to show mercy to His servant, He casts that confession into his heart, and mercy comes with it. This is especially so when the servant's confession is joined with a firm resolve never to return to what displeases his Lord. Allah knows that this has entered his heart and its innermost core, and mercy does not fail to accompany it. In the *Mu'jam* of al-Tabarani, from the hadith of Yazid ibn Sinan al-Rahawi, from Sulayman ibn Amir, from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The last man to enter Paradise is a man who will be crawling on the Sirat, face down and then face up, like a boy whom his father beats and who flees from him. His deeds will fail him in his effort to move forward, so he will say: 'O Lord, bring me to Paradise and save me from the Fire.' Allah, blessed and exalted, will reveal to him: 'My servant, if I save you from the Fire and admit you to Paradise, will you confess to Me your sins and transgressions?' The servant will say: 'Yes, O Lord, by Your might and majesty, if You save me from the Fire I will surely confess to You my sins and transgressions.' He will then cross the bridge, and the servant will say to himself: 'If I confess my sins and transgressions to Him, He will surely return me to the Fire.' Allah will reveal to him: 'My servant, confess to Me your sins and transgressions, and I will forgive them for you and admit you to Paradise.' The servant will say: 'No, by Your might and majesty, I have never committed a sin, nor ever made a mistake.' Allah will reveal to him: 'My servant, I have a witness against you.' The servant will look right and left and see no one, and will say: 'O Lord, show me Your witness.' Allah, exalted, will then make his skin speak of his minor transgressions. When the servant sees that, he will say: 'O Lord, I have with me, by Your might, the grave ones.' Allah will reveal to him: 'My servant, I know them better than you do. Confess them to Me, and I will forgive them for you and admit you to Paradise.' The servant will then confess his sins, and he will enter Paradise." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed, and said: "This is the lowest-ranked person of Paradise; how about the one above him?"

So the Lord, blessed and exalted, desires from His servant confession, humility before Him, submission, lowliness toward Him, and resolve to seek His pleasure. As long as the people of the Fire lack this spirit, they lack mercy. When Allah, mighty and majestic, wills to show mercy to them, or to some of them, He places this in their hearts, and mercy overtakes them. The power of the Lord, blessed and exalted, is not deficient in this, and there is nothing in it that contradicts what His names and attributes require. He has informed us that He is "one who does whatever He wills."

The twenty-second aspect: Allah, glorified and exalted, has made eternal abiding (*khulud*) the consequence of major sins and has restricted it by eternity (*ta'bid*). That eternity does not preclude its cessation and ending. Among the verses is His saying: ﴿Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment.﴾ Among the hadiths is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever kills himself with an iron implement, that implement will be in his hand, with which he will stab his belly in the Fire of Hell, abiding there forever, eternally." This is a sound hadith. Likewise is his statement in another hadith concerning one who kills himself: Allah, blessed and exalted, says: "My servant hastened to take his own life, so Paradise is forbidden to him." And more emphatic than this is His saying: ﴿Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.﴾ This is a threat restricted by abiding and eternity, though it is definitively terminated by the servant's own act, which is monotheism (*tawhid*). Likewise, the general threat against the people of the Fire does not preclude its cessation through the one who has prescribed mercy upon Himself, whose mercy overcomes His wrath. Had the disbeliever known all the mercy that is with Allah, he would not despair of His mercy, as in Sahih al-Bukhari, from him (ﷺ): "Allah created mercy on the day He created it as one hundred mercies." He said at its end: "If the disbeliever knew all that is with Allah of mercy, he would not despair of Paradise; and if the Muslim knew all that is with Allah of punishment, he would not feel safe from the Fire."

The twenty-third aspect: if a report had come from Him, glorified and exalted, explicitly stating that the punishment of the Fire has no end and is everlasting without cessation, that would be a threat from Him, glorified and exalted. Allah, exalted, does not break His promise. As for threats, the position of all the People of the Sunnah is that failing to carry them out is generosity, pardon and forgiveness, by which the Lord, blessed and exalted, is praised and commended. For a threat is His right: if He wills, He leaves it, and if He wills, He exacts it. A generous one does not exact his right, so how much more so the Most Generous of the generous? He, glorified and exalted, has declared in His Book, in more than one place, that He does not break His promise, and He did not say in a single place that He does not break His threat. Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili reported: Hadbah ibn Khalid related to us, Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm related to us, Thabit al-Bunani related to us, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah promises a reward for an action, He will fulfil it for him; and whoever He threatens with punishment for an action, He has the choice."

Abu al-Shaykh al-Isbahani said: Muhammad ibn Hamzah related to us, Ahmad ibn al-Khalil related to us, al-Asma'i related to us: 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd came to Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' and said: "O Abu 'Amr, does Allah break what He promised?" He said: "No." He said: "What do you think of one whom Allah threatens with punishment for his deed; will Allah break His threat against him?" Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: "From barbarity have you come, O Abu 'Uthman. The promise is not the threat. The Arabs do not regard it as shameful or a breach when one threatens evil and then does not carry it out; they regard that as generosity and virtue. Breaking is only when one promises good and then does not do it." He said: "Show me this in the speech of the Arabs." He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the words of the ancient poet:

*And the paternal cousin does not fear my might, as long as I live,
nor do I fear the attack of the menacer.*

*Indeed, whether I threaten him or promise him,
I break my threat and fulfil my promise.*"

Abu al-Shaykh said: Yahya ibn Mu'adh said: "The promise and the threat are both rights. The promise is the servant's right upon Allah: He guaranteed them that if they do such and such, He will give them such and such. And who is more worthy of fulfilling than Allah? The threat is His right upon the servants: He said, 'Do not do such and such, or I will punish you.' They did it. If He wills, He pardons, and if He wills, He exacts, because it is His right." And the more fitting of the two for our Lord, blessed and exalted, is pardon and generosity: ﴿Indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Something that confirms this and supports it is the report of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr, when the Messenger (ﷺ) threatened him, and he said:

*I have been told that the Messenger of Allah threatened me,
but pardon from the Messenger of Allah is to be hoped for.*

If this is so for an unrestricted threat, how much more so for a threat joined with an exception, followed by His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is one who does whatever He wills.﴾ This is His report that He does what He wills after His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills.﴾ So it necessarily refers back to Him. It cannot refer only to the thing excepted; rather it either concerns the excepted case alone or refers to both. It is clear that its connection to His saying "except what your Lord wills" is more fitting than its connection to "abiding therein." This is evident to the one who reflects. This is also what the Companions understood. They said: this verse came in the threats of the Qur'an, and they did not mean the exception alone, for the exception is also mentioned in al-An'am. They meant that it follows the exception with His saying ﴿Indeed your Lord is one who does whatever He wills.﴾ This sequence is like His saying in al-An'am: ﴿abiding therein, except what your Lord wills. Indeed your Lord is Wise, Knowing.﴾ Thus He informs us that their punishment is in all times, and that He lifts it from them at a time He wills, arising from His perfect knowledge and wisdom, not from a bare will detached from wisdom, benefit, mercy and justice, since His will cannot be detached from these.

The twenty-fourth aspect: the side of mercy prevails in this transient, perishing, quickly vanishing world over the side of punishment and wrath. Had it not been so, it would not have been inhabited, nor would it have subsisted. As Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And if Allah were to seize people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature.﴾ And He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back a single creature.﴾ So were it not for the vastness of His mercy, His forgiveness and His pardon, the world would not stand. Despite this, what He has manifested of mercy in this abode and sent down among the creatures is one part of a hundred parts of mercy. If the side of mercy has prevailed in this abode and has reached the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever, even though the requirement of punishment is present, and they engage in it and are empowered to anger their Lord and strive toward His displeasure, how then would the side of mercy not prevail in an abode where mercy is multiplied over that of this abode by ninety-nine times? The punishment has taken its full effect upon the disbelievers; those souls have been broken, the punishment has worn them out, and it has melted away from them evil and wickedness. Yet it did not prevent His mercy toward them in this world; rather He showed them mercy while the requirement of punishment and wrath was still in them. How much more so when the requirement of wrath and punishment has ceased, and the side of mercy has grown many times over the mercy of this abode, and the evil and wickedness that were in it have vanished, the Fire having melted and consumed them. The secret of the matter is this: the names of mercy and beneficence are more prevalent, more manifest and more numerous than the names of vengeance; the act of mercy is more frequent than the act of vengeance; the traces of mercy are greater than the traces of vengeance; and mercy is more beloved to Him than vengeance. By mercy He created His creation, and for it He created them. It is mercy that preceded His wrath and overcame it, and He prescribed it upon Himself, and it encompasses all things. What was created by mercy is desired for its own sake, while what was created by wrath is willed for the sake of something else, as has been established earlier. Punishment is discipline and purification, while mercy is beneficence, generosity and bounty; punishment is treatment, while mercy is giving and bestowal.

The twenty-fifth aspect: Allah, glorified and exalted, will necessarily make manifest to all His creatures on the Day of Resurrection His truthfulness and the truthfulness of His messengers, and that His enemies were the liars and the fabricators. He will make manifest to them His judgment, which is the most just judgment against His enemies, and that He judged concerning them a judgment which they themselves will praise, let alone His friends, His angels and His messengers; so that the whole cosmos speaks the praise: "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds." For this reason He, exalted, says: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said, "All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ The subject of the saying has been omitted to indicate generality, and that this is uttered on the tongue of every speaker and in the heart of every one. Al-Hasan said: "They entered the Fire while their hearts were full of praise of Him, though they found no way to it." This is what made it good to omit the subject in His saying: ﴿It will be said: enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein.﴾ So that the whole cosmos is the one saying it to them, since it is His just judgment concerning them, and the requirement of His wisdom and praise. As for the people of Paradise, He, exalted, says: ﴿And its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you are good, so enter it, abiding."﴾ They did not deserve it by their deeds; they deserved it only through His pardon, mercy and bounty. So when Allah, glorified and exalted, makes His angels and all creatures witness His just judgment and His overwhelming wisdom, placing the punishment where the intellects, the natural dispositions and creation testify that it is the most fitting and worthy place for it, and that this is part of the perfection of His praise, which is the requirement of His names and attributes, and that these wicked, unjust, corrupt souls deserve nothing other than this and nothing else is fitting for them, to the point that they themselves acknowledge that they deserve it and are most worthy of it, then the wisdom for which evil and its causes came into being in this abode and that abode is fulfilled. There is nothing in the divine wisdom that evils should remain forever with no end or cessation, so that they and the goods would be on an equal footing.
