This is the furthest point reached by both groups in this question, and perhaps you will not find it outside this book. If it is asked, "Where do you end your steps in this matter of great importance, which is greater than this world by manifold multiples?" The answer: at His saying, blessed and exalted, ﴿Indeed your Lord is one who does whatever He wills.﴾ And to this point the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), advanced in it, when he mentioned the entry of the people of Paradise into Paradise and the people of the Fire into the Fire, and what each of these groups encounters, and he said: "Then Allah will do after that whatever He wills."

[The Third and Twenty-Third Chapter: On Presenting the Objections of Those Who Deny Wisdom and Causation in God's Acts, and the Responses to Them]

They say: The Lord, exalted is He, has named Himself the Forgiving, the Merciful, and He has not named Himself the Punisher or the Retributor. Rather, He placed punishment and retribution among His acts, as He says: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾. And He says: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in retribution, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. And He says: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe. Indeed, it is He who originates and restores, and He is the Forgiving, the Loving﴾. And He says: ﴿Ha, Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing, Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in retribution﴾.

This is abundant in the Qur'an. He, glorified is He, praises Himself with pardon, forgiveness, mercy, generosity and forbearance, and names Himself accordingly, but He does not praise Himself as the Retributor, nor as the Angry, nor as the Punisher, nor as the Afflicter, except in the hadith that enumerates the Most Beautiful Names, and that hadith is not authentically established.

And He has prescribed for Himself in a book that His mercy precedes His wrath.

Likewise, regarding the people of the Fire, His mercy towards them precedes His wrath. For He showed them mercy in various forms before they angered Him with their polytheism; He showed them mercy in their state of polytheism; He showed them mercy by establishing the proof against them; and He showed them mercy by calling them to Himself after they had angered Him, harmed His messengers and denied them. He gave them respite and did not hasten to punish them. Rather, His mercy encompassed them. So His mercy overcame His wrath. Had it not been so, the world would have been ruined, the heavens would have fallen upon the earth, and the mountains would have collapsed. And when mercy is dominant over wrath and precedes it, it is impossible that the cause of wrath should be permanent by its permanence, overcoming His mercy.

They say: Punishment is either pointless, or it is for a benefit and wisdom. That it be pointless is something the Most Wise of the wise is exalted above, and attributing it to Him is attributing to Him one of the greatest deficiencies.

And if it is for a benefit, then benefit means gain, along with its necessary consequences and what it necessitates; this benefit either returns to the Lord, exalted is He, and He is exalted above that and sanctified beyond it;

or it returns to the creature: either the punished person himself, or another, or both.

The first is impossible, for there is no benefit to him in the perpetuation of punishment without end.

As for the benefit of another: if it is admonition and deterrence, then it has been achieved. If it is the completion of his pleasure, joy and happiness, by seeing his enemy in that state while he is in the utmost bliss, then this, even if he were the harshest of creatures, would soften him toward his enemy because of the length of his torment and the permanence of what he suffers. Nothing remains except breaking those arrogant, stubborn souls and treating them so that they reach the root of their diseases and maladies, and thus cut them off. And that root is an evil that came upon a good nature in which they were created at the beginning of their innate disposition.

They say: The possible divisions concerning creation are five, with no more beyond them: pure good and its opposite; predominant good and its opposite; good and evil equal; and wisdom requires the existence of two of them, namely pure good and predominant good.

As for pure evil or predominant evil, wisdom does not require its existence; rather, it rejects that. For everything Allah, glorified is He, has created, He created for a wisdom whose existence is better than its non-existence. And He created harmful creatures and actions that are evil because of the beloved good that follows from their creation. So He did not create for mere evil that entails no good in any respect; this is the utmost impossibility.

Good is the thing intended in itself, by the primary intention, while evil is intended only as a means and a starting point, not as an ultimate goal and final end. Then when the intended end is achieved by its creation, it passes away and ceases, just as means cease upon reaching their ends, as is known by sense and reason. On this basis, punishment is evil, and it has an end sought through it, and it is a means to that end. So when its purpose is achieved, it becomes like the road that leads to the destination: when the traveler has reached his goal, there is no further use in traversing it.

The essence of the matter is that mercy is the goal of creation and command, not punishment. Punishment is among His creations, and this is consistent with His having created it for a praiseworthy end, and with the necessity of the manifestation of His names and the effect of His attributes in generality and absoluteness, for this is perfection, and the Lord, majestic is His majesty, is described as perfect and exalted above deficiency.

They say: Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾. And He said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills﴾. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: "This verse overrides every verse in the Qur'an." Related by al-Bayhaqi, Harb and others.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "There will come upon Hell a time when no one is in it, and that is after they have remained in it for ages (ahqab)." Similar is related from Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Hurayrah, mentioned by a group of authors of the Sunnah.

This implies that the abode in which no one remains is the one in which its people remain for ages.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Allah informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, but He did not inform us of what He wills for the people of the Fire."

They say: What suffices us is what is in Surah al-An'am, His saying: ﴿And the Day He will gather them all: "O company of jinn, you have taken much of mankind," and their allies from mankind will say, "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us." He will say, "The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing"﴾, up to His saying: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did not messengers from among you come to you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say, "We testify against ourselves." And the worldly life deceived them, and they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers﴾.

This is addressed to the disbelievers among the jinn and mankind in several respects.

First: their being arrogant toward them, meaning toward their seducers and misleaders; they were only arrogant toward the disbelievers.

Second: His saying: ﴿And their allies from mankind will say﴾; and their allies are the disbelievers, as He says: ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾. So the party of Satan are his allies.

Third: His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾. And despite this, He said: ﴿The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills﴾. Then He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing﴾. So their punishment is tied to His knowledge and wisdom, and likewise the exception proceeds from knowledge and wisdom; He is Knowing of what He does to them and Wise in that.

They say: It has come in the Qur'an that when He mentions the reward of the people of His mercy and the people of His wrath together, He makes the reward of the people of mercy eternal and leaves the reward of the people of wrath unrestricted, as in His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends. As for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills, a gift never cut off﴾. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved from among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the Fire of Hell, abiding therein. They are the worst of creation. Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, they are the best of creation. Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾. And His saying: ﴿On a Day when faces will turn white and faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turned black: "Did you disbelieve after your belief? So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve." And as for those whose faces turned white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, abiding therein eternally﴾.

Sometimes He mentions them together and decrees eternity for them, as in His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, then for him is the Fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾, and His saying: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, abiding therein, and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾. But mere mention of abiding and eternity does not necessitate the absence of an end; rather, abiding is a long stay, as they say: "a long-lasting chain (qayd mukhallad)," and the eternity of each thing is according to its kind. Eternity may be for the duration of life, and it may be for the duration of the worldly life. He said concerning the Jews: ﴿And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth; and Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾. And it is known that they will wish for it in the Fire, when they say: ﴿O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us﴾. The non-cessation of the bliss of Paradise is derived only from His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision, which has no end﴾, and His saying: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, and His saying: ﴿for them is a reward never interrupted﴾, meaning uncut.

Whoever says it is not bestowed upon them as a favour has erred in the worst error. Nothing like this has come concerning the punishment of the people of the Fire.

And His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿They will not be removed from the Fire﴾, ﴿nor will they be brought out of it﴾, and His saying: ﴿It will not be decreed for them that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾, and His exalted saying: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it﴾ in two places of the Qur'an, and His saying: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins than them﴾. (All of these are) not diverted from their apparent meaning and literal reality, according to the correct view.

Some have claimed that the unrestricted wording of these verses is qualified by the verses that restrict it with the exception of God's will, so that it is a case of specifying the general. This resembles the view of some of the early scholars who said that the verse of exception overrides every threat in the Qur'an.

The correct view is that these verses are on their general and unrestricted sense, but there is nothing in them indicating that the Fire itself is permanent by the permanence of God, with no end. Nothing in the Qur'an or the Sunnah indicates this in any way.

There is a difference between the punishment of its people being permanent as long as it lasts, and the Fire itself being everlasting, never ceasing, never perishing. These are two different things.

It may be said: On this view there is no difference between the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, since each of them perishes and ends?

It is said: The differences between them are too clear to need stating, and the matter is more evident than to require a distinction.

Furthermore, the punishment of this world ends with the death of the one punished and the lifting of the punishment from him. But as for the punishment of the Hereafter, the one who deserves to abide in it does not die, the punishment is not lifted from him, and no one repels it from him, as He says: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to befall, none can avert it﴾. It is constant and does not depart. He says: ﴿Indeed, its punishment was ever a constant torment﴾, meaning constant; and from this the creditor (gharim) is so named because of the constancy of his claim upon his debtor.

(Section)

As for the reports on this question: al-Tabarani said, narrating: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salm narrated to us, Sahl ibn Uthman narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Mis'ar ibn Kidam narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ): "There will certainly come upon Hell a day when it is like a dry, arid field, its doors banging."

Harb said in his Masa'il: "I asked Ishaq: I said, regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾ —

He said: This verse covers every threat in the Qur'an."

Abd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: my father said: Abu Nadrah narrated to us, from Jabir, or Abu Sa'id, or one of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "This verse covers the entire Qur'an: ﴿except as your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾."

Mu'tamir said: "He said: every threat in the Qur'an." Then Harb interpreted it, saying: "Its meaning according to me — and Allah knows best — is that it covers every threat in the Qur'an addressed to the people of monotheism, and likewise His saying: ﴿except as your Lord wills﴾ makes an exception for those of the qibla who will leave the Fire."

This interpretation is not sound, because the exception is only regarding the threat to the disbelievers. For He, glorified is He, said: ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission; among them are the wretched and the happy. As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾, the verse continuing: ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise﴾. So the people of monotheism are among those who were made happy, not the wretched. And the verse of al-An'am is explicit regarding the disbelievers, as has been explained earlier.

Harb said: And Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu ... Malih narrated to us, he heard Umar ibn Maymun relating from Abd Allah ibn Amr who said: "There will certainly come upon Hell a day when its doors clatter, with no one in it, and that is after they have remained in it for ages."

Ubayd Allah narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah who said: "As for what I say, that there will come upon Hell a day when no one remains in it" — and he recited (As for those who were wretched, they are in the Fire) — the verse.

Ubayd Allah said: "Our companions used to say: it means the monotheists." It has already been stated that this interpretation is not sound.

Abd ibn Humayd said in his Tafsir: Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from al-Hasan, who said: Umar said: "If the people of the Fire remained in the Fire for a number of grains of the sands of 'Alij, there would still be a day for them on which they would come out."

And he said: Hajjaj ibn Minhal informed us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, that Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "If the people of the Fire remained in the Fire for the number of grains of the sands of 'Alij, there would be a day for them on which they would come out."

The narrators of this report are all trustworthy imams. Al-Hasan heard it from some of the Successors and related it without denouncing it. This indicates that the report circulated among these imams without any objection from them. They used to denounce anyone who departed even slightly from the Sunnah, and they narrated reports refuting such deviations. Imam Ahmad used to say: "The narrations of Hammad ibn Salamah are the bone stuck in the throats of the innovators." So if this view had been among them a innovation contrary to the Sunnah and consensus, they would have hastened to reject and denounce it.

In the Tafsir of Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing﴾, he said: "It is not fitting for anyone to pass judgment on Allah regarding His creation, nor to place them in Paradise or in the Fire."

Al-Tabari said: "It has been related from Ibn Abbas that he interpreted this exception to mean that God made the matter of these people, in the extent of His punishment of them, subject to His will." This statement from Ibn Abbas refutes the view of those who interpreted the verse to mean something other than: except what God wills of various kinds of punishment; or who said the meaning is: except the duration of their stay before entering, from the time they were raised until they entered; or that it refers to the people of the qibla; or that "ma" means "man" (who); or that it means "waw" (and), i.e., "and what Allah wills." All of these are cold, weak interpretations unfitting for the verse, and whoever reflects upon them will be certain of their falsehood.

Al-Suddi said concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿remaining therein for ages (ahqab)﴾: "Seven hundred ahqab, each ahqab seventy years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day like a thousand years of what you count." The specifying of their stay therein by ages indicates a determined period limited by number. This is the view of most scholars. For this reason al-Zajjaj interpreted the verse as meaning that the ages qualify His saying "they will not taste therein coolness or drink," while the duration of their stay is not measured by ages. This is a corrupt interpretation, for it implies that after the ages they would be tasting coolness and drink.

Another group said the verse is abrogated by His saying: ﴿They will not be removed from it﴾ and His saying: ﴿They will abide therein﴾.

This too is corrupt. If by abrogation they mean lifting (raf'), it does not apply to a statement of information unless it has the sense of a command. If by abrogation they mean clarification (bayan), then it is correct, and it indicates only that their punishment is continuous and lasting as long as the Fire endures: they abide therein, and they will not be removed. This is a known truth, supported by the evidence of the Qur'an and the Sunnah. But the issue is something else: whether the Fire is everlasting and permanent by the permanence of the Lord. Where is the evidence for this from the Qur'an or the Sunnah in any way whatsoever?

Another group said the verse concerns the people of monotheism. This is more repugnant than what preceded it, and the context of the verses rejects it outright. When those who saw the falsity of these interpretations said: the mention of ahqab does not indicate an end, for they are not limited by a number. For He did not say ten or a hundred; and even if they were limited by a number, it would not indicate an end except by implication, so how much more so when they are not limited? They said: the meaning of the verse is that whenever one ahqab passes, another ahqab follows it, without end.

This claim is not supported by the verse in any way. As for their claim that the periods (*ahqab*) are not fixed: if the verse were meant to show that the duration of the punishment has no end, it would not have been restricted to *ahqab*. Something without end is not described as lasting for *ahqab*, *dahr*, *a'sar*, or the like. For this reason one does not say this about the bliss of the people of Paradise, nor does one say of an everlasting thing that does not cease that it lasts for *ahqab* or thousands of years. The Companions understood the meanings of the Qur'an better than anyone. Yet 'Umar ibn al-Khattab understood the verse differently from them, just as Ibn 'Abbas understood the exception clause differently from them. The understanding of the Companions regarding the Qur'an is the ultimate reference on which one relies.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "There will certainly come upon Jahannam (Hell) a time when its gates will swing, with no one in it, after they have remained in it for *ahqab*."

Ibn Jarir said, relating from al-Musayyib, from one he mentioned, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills﴾: "God commanded the Fire to consume them."

He said: "And Ibn Mas'ud said, [and] he mentioned it." He also said: "Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Jahannam is the faster of the two abodes to be built and the faster of the two to be ruined.'"

I say: His statement "the faster of the two to be ruined" does not indicate the ruin of the other abode, as in His saying, ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day are better in their resting place and finer in their resort﴾, and His saying, ﴿Is God better, or what they associate [with Him]?﴾, and His saying in the hadith: "God is higher and greater."

His statement "the faster of the two to be built" may have two meanings:
One: the people's haste toward the deeds that lead them into Jahannam, and their slowness toward the deeds of the Hereafter.
The second: its people enter it before the people of Paradise enter theirs. The people of Paradise only enter it after crossing the Sirat (the bridge over Hell) and after being held back at the bridge beyond it, whereas the people of the Fire have already taken their places in it, for they do not cross the Sirat and are not held at that bridge.

Also, in the sound hadith: "When the caller calls out: 'Let every nation follow what it used to worship,' the polytheists follow their idols and deities, and they fall into the Fire with them. This nation remains at the place of standing until their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, comes to them and says: 'Will you not go where the people have gone?'"

Al-Khatib mentioned in his *Tarikh*, in the biography of Sahl ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Dawud ibn Sulayman Abu Nasr al-Bukhari: Muhammad ibn Nuh al-Jundisaburi narrated to us, Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Naqid narrated to us, Sahl ibn 'Uthman narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Mis'ar ibn Kidam narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:
"A day will come upon Jahannam when no one from the children of Adam will be in it, and its gates will swing as if they were the gates of the monotheists."

The reliance is not on this alone, for its chain is weak. It has been related through another route from Ibn Mas'ud, which has already been mentioned.

(Section)

As for those who are certain that the Fire is everlasting and will never perish, they have several approaches.

The first: the verses and hadiths that indicate their abiding therein, that they will not die, that "they will not be removed from it" (Qur'an 5:37), that death will be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire, and that the disbelievers will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. These and similar texts do not indicate what they claim. They only show that as long as the Fire remains, they will be in it. Where in them is there anything that indicates its non-annihilation?

The second approach: the claim of consensus (*ijma'*) on this matter. We have already mentioned, from the statements of the Companions and the Followers, what shows the matter is contrary to what they claim, to the extent that someone claimed the consensus of the Companions on this side, based on those reports, of which no contrary opinion from them is known.

The third approach: it is known as a matter of necessity from the religion of Islam that Paradise and the Fire will not perish, but both remain. For this reason, all the People of the Sunnah denounced Abu al-Hudhayl, Jahm, and their followers who said that the Fire perishes, and they counted their views among the innovations that oppose what the Messenger brought. There is no doubt that this is one of the innovations by which they left the Sunnah. But from where can the claim of theoretical knowledge be valid that the Fire remains by God's remaining and endures by His enduring, let alone necessary knowledge? Where in the textual or rational evidence is there even one proof that requires this?

The fourth approach: the widespread or mass-transmitted Sunnah has reported the exit of the people of tawhid (monotheism) from the Fire, but not the disbelievers. This is known from the Sunnah with certainty. What they say is true beyond doubt, but the people of tawhid exited from it while it remained, it did not perish or cease to exist. The disbelievers do not obtain this; rather they remain in it as long as it remains.

The fifth approach: reason indicates the eternal abiding of the disbelievers in it and their not leaving it. Their souls are not receptive to good, for if they were to leave it they would return to disbelief as they were. God, the Exalted, pointed to this in His saying: ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ (Qur'an 6:28). This indicates the utmost of their obstinacy and persistence and the absence of acceptance of good in them in any way. Their wicked, corrupt souls are fit only for punishment, and if they were fit, they would have become fit after a long punishment. Since their punishment over those long periods has not affected their souls or made them good, it is known that there is no receptivity to good in them at all, and that the causes of the punishment have not been removed from their souls, so the punishment that follows from them will not be lifted. This approach, although it may be rejected at first glance, is a strong approach, and it returns to the approach of wisdom: the wisdom that required their entry is the same wisdom that requires their eternal abiding. But this approach is forbidden to those who deny wisdom and to those who affirm it among the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school) and the Qadariyyah (who affirm human free will and divine justice in a rationalist manner). As for the deniers, it is obvious.

As for the affirmers: for them, wisdom is that their punishment is for their own benefit. This is only valid if they have two states: a state in which they are punished for their own benefit, and a state in which the punishment is removed so that that benefit is achieved. Otherwise, how could their benefit lie in a punishment that never ends? As for one who affirms a wisdom that returns to the Lord, the Exalted, they can take this approach. But it may be said: wisdom does not require that their punishment last as long as His existence endures, and He has not informed us that He created them for that. They are punished for a praiseworthy purpose, and when it is achieved, the goal of their punishment is attained. He, glory be to Him, does not punish His creation in vain. He is able to bring them into a new creation after the long punishment, free from those evils and corruptions that were in their souls, which the long punishment has removed. For they were created receptive to good by nature (*fitrah*), and this receptivity is inherent in their creation, and by it they acknowledged their Creator and Originator. What came upon it was only something that nullified its requirement. When that accidental factor is removed by the long punishment, the original receptivity remains without opposition.

As for His saying, ﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾, this refers to before they endured the punishment. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say, "Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." But rather, there has become apparent to them what they had concealed before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ (Qur'an 6:27–28).

So those evils and corruptions remain established in their souls; the Fire has not removed them. If they were returned, they would revert, because the cause for returning remains. But where did He, glory be to Him, inform that if He were to return them after the long, everlasting punishment, they would return to what they were forbidden? The secret of the matter is that original nature (*fitrah*) must do its work, just as the accidental factor did its work. This *fitrah* is common to all the children of Adam, as in the two Sahihs (*Sahih al-Bukhari* and *Sahih Muslim*), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Every child is born upon the *fitrah*," and in another wording, "upon this religion (*millah*)." And in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of 'Iyad ibn Himar al-Mujashi'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding what he relates from his Lord, He said:
"I created My servants as *hunafa'* (upright monotheists), all of them, and the devils came to them and led them away from their religion, and commanded them to associate with Me what I have not sent down any authority for."

So He informed that the basis for them is *hanifiyyah* (pure monotheism), that they were created upon it, and that its obstruction is an accidental factor that came to them through the devils seizing them away from it. It is impossible that the effect of the devils' seizing them should operate while the effect of the creation of the Merciful, majestic is great, does not operate. Everything is His creation, glory be to Him; there is no creator besides Him. But that creation is one He loves and is pleased with, and its effect is attributed to Him. And this creation is one He hates and is angry with, and its effect is not attributed to Him, for evil is not from Him, and all good is in His hands.

If it is said: He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾ (Qur'an 8:23). This implies that there is no receptivity in them and no good whatsoever with them, and if there were good with them, they would have come out of the Fire with the monotheists, for He, glory be to Him, brings out from the Fire whoever has in his heart even the least, least, weight of a mustard seed of good. So it is known that these people do not have this slight amount of good?

It is said: The good in this hadith is faith in God and His messengers, as in the other wording, "the least, least, least weight of a mustard seed of faith," which is affirming His messengers and submitting to them with the heart and the limbs. As for the good in the verse, what is meant is acceptance, purification, knowing the extent of the blessing, and thanking the Benefactor for it. If God, glory be to Him, knew this in them, He would have made them hear in a way that would benefit them, for they heard a hearing by which the proof was established against them. That receptivity has lost its effect and has been rendered inoperative by disbelief and denial, and it has become like a non-existent thing that gives no benefit. Its effect appeared only in the establishment of the proof against them, and its effect did not appear in their benefiting from what they did and were certain of.

If it is said: The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed on the day he was sealed as a disbeliever, and Nuh said regarding his people: ﴿and they will not beget except a wicked disbeliever﴾ (Qur'an 71:27). And in the hadith related by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The children of Adam were created in different categories: some are born believers, live as believers, and die as believers; and some are born disbelievers, live as disbelievers, and die as disbelievers," the hadith...

It is said: This does not contradict that he was born upon the *fitrah*, for he was sealed and born with his disbelief decreed, to be actualized when he reached understanding. Otherwise, at the time of his birth he knows neither disbelief nor faith. That state is one of decree, not one in which the agent is present. So he was born upon the *fitrah* and born a disbeliever in two correct, established senses. The first is by acceptance and preference for Islam, if left alone. The second is by action and will, once he reaches understanding. So if you combine the preceding *fitrah*, the preceding mercy, the lofty wisdom, and the complete self-sufficiency, and you pair his *fitrah* with His mercy, His wisdom, and His self-sufficiency, the matter will become clear to you.

The sixth approach: analogizing the abode of justice to the abode of grace, and that just as the latter is everlasting, so is the former, because the latter requires His justice, and His justice and mercy are among the necessary attributes of His essence. This approach is not valid. Justice is His right, glory be to Him; He is not obliged to fulfill it, and no deficiency or blame attaches to Him in any way by leaving it. Grace is His promise, which He made to His servants and made binding upon Himself. There are many differences between the two abodes, both in revelation and in reason.

The first: God, the Exalted, informed that the bliss of Paradise has no end, that the gift of its people is not cut off, and that it is not "unending" (Qur'an 11:108). This has not come regarding the punishment of the people of the Fire.

The second: He informed of what indicates the end of the punishment of the people of the Fire in a number of verses, as has been mentioned, and He did not inform of anything indicating the end of the bliss of the people of Paradise. For this reason, those who hold to perpetual, never-ending eternity needed to interpret those verses, while nothing regarding the bliss of the people of Paradise has come that requires them to specify it by interpretation.

The third: none of the hadiths that came regarding the end of the punishment of the Fire have come regarding the end of the bliss of Paradise.

The fourth: the Companions and the Followers mentioned only the cessation of the punishment, and none of them mentioned the cessation of the bliss.

The fifth: it is established that God enters people into Paradise without any deed at all, unlike the Fire.

The sixth: He creates in Paradise a creation whom He blesses there, and He does not create in the Fire a creation whom He punishes there.

The seventh: Paradise is a requirement of His mercy, and the Fire is a requirement of His wrath. Those who enter the Fire are many times over those who enter Paradise. If the punishment of these people lasted as long as the bliss of those people, His wrath would overcome His mercy, and wrath would be the dominant and preceding attribute, which is impossible.

The eighth: Paradise is the abode of His grace, and the Fire is the abode of His justice, and His grace overcomes His justice.

The ninth: the Fire is the abode of exacting what is His due, and Paradise is the abode of fulfilling the right He made binding upon Himself. He, glory be to Him, forgoes His own right, but He does not forgo the right He made binding upon Himself.

The tenth: Paradise is the ultimate purpose for which they were created in the Hereafter, and their deeds are the ultimate purpose for which they were created in this world. This is unlike the Fire, for He, glory be to Him, did not create His creation to disbelieve in Him or to associate others with Him, but He created them to worship Him and that He might show them mercy.

The eleventh: bliss is required by His names and attributes, whereas punishment is only from His acts. God, the Exalted, said: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ (Qur'an 15:49–50). And He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (Qur'an 7:167). And He said: ﴿Know that God is severe in punishment and that God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (Qur'an 5:98). Whatever is required by His names and attributes endures as long as they endure.

If it is said: Punishment proceeds from His might, wisdom, and justice, and these are the Most Beautiful Names and attributes of perfection. So should what proceeds from them not endure as long as they endure?

It is said: By the life of God, punishment did proceed from might, wisdom, and justice, and its ending when its purpose is achieved also proceeds from might, wisdom, and justice. Neither the punishment nor its cessation departs from His might, wisdom, and justice. Rather, at its ending, there is might accompanied by mercy, and wisdom accompanied by generosity, benevolence, pardon, and forgiveness. Might and wisdom have never ceased and have not diminished; rather, all that He created, creates, and commands, and commands, proceeds from His might and wisdom.

The twelfth: punishment is intended for something else, not for itself, whereas mercy, benevolence, and bliss are intended for themselves. Benevolence and bliss are the end, while punishment and pain are a means. How can one be measured by the other?

The thirteenth: He, glory be to Him, informed that His mercy encompasses everything, that His mercy precedes His wrath, and that He prescribed mercy upon Himself. So His mercy must encompass these punished people. If they remained in punishment without an end, His mercy would not encompass them, and this is very clear.

If it is said: He, glory be to Him, said right after it: ﴿So I will prescribe it for those who fear Him﴾ (Qur'an 7:156), and so, to the end of the verse, others will be excluded from it, because they have departed from the attribute by which they deserve it?

It is said: The mercy prescribed for these people is not the all-encompassing mercy for all creation, but a specific mercy by which He singled them out, apart from others, and prescribed it for them rather than for anyone else. They are the people of success who are not punished but are the people of mercy, triumph, and bliss. The mention of the particular after the general is by way of digression (*istitrad*), and this is common in the Qur'an. Indeed, it may digress from the particular to the general, as in His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquility in her. And when he covered her, she bore a light burden and carried it around. But when it became heavy, they both called upon God, their Lord, "If You give us a righteous one, we will surely be among the grateful"﴾ (Qur'an 7:189). This is a digression from mention of the parents to mention of the offspring. And from the digression in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of the stars and made them as missiles against the devils﴾ (Qur'an 37:6–7). Those made as missiles are not the same as those with which the sky was adorned, but He digressed from mention of one kind to another kind, and He returned a pronoun referring to the second to the first, because both come under one genus. Likewise His saying: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Him﴾ (Qur'an 7:156). What is prescribed for those who fear Him is a specific kind of the all-encompassing mercy. The point is that mercy must encompass the people of the Fire, and it must end where knowledge ends, as the angels said: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge﴾ (Qur'an 40:7).

The fourteenth: it is authentically established from him (ﷺ) in the hadith of intercession: "The speech of the Possessors of Resolve (*ulu al-'azm*): 'Indeed my Lord has become angry today with an anger the like of which He has never been angry before, and He will never be angry after it the like of it.'"

This is explicit that this great anger does not endure. It is known that the people of the Fire entered it only because of that anger, so if that anger lasted, their punishment would last, since it is the requirement of that anger. When the Lord, blessed and exalted, becomes pleased and that anger is removed, its requirement is removed. This is like the general punishments and afflictions of this world, which are the effects of His anger: when His anger persists, that affliction persists; when He becomes pleased and His anger is removed, the affliction is removed and mercy takes its place.

**The fifteenth:** His good pleasure is more beloved to Him than His wrath, His pardon is more beloved to Him than His punishment, His mercy is more beloved to Him than His torment, and His giving is more beloved to Him than His withholding. Wrath, punishment, and withholding occur only through causes that contradict what those attributes and names require. He, glorified is He, loves His names and attributes as He loves their effects and what they necessitate, as in the hadith: "He is Witr (the One) and loves the odd number; Beautiful and loves beauty; Clean and loves cleanliness; Pardoning and loves pardon." He is Grateful and loves the grateful; All-Knowing and loves those who seek knowledge; Generous and loves the generous; Modest and Concealing and loves those who are modest and conceal; Patient and loves the patient; Merciful and loves the merciful. So He dislikes whatever opposes these. Likewise, He hates disbelief, disobedience, sinfulness, injustice, and ignorance, because these qualities oppose the qualities of His perfection, which accord with His names and attributes. Yet He wills them, glorified is He, because they necessitate what He loves and is pleased with. So He wills them as necessary consequences that are intended for something else, since they are a disobedience that leads to what He loves. When what He loves is achieved through them and they lead to the end He intends, glorified is He, they are no longer intended either for themselves or for something else. They then cease, and their opposites replace them, which are more beloved to Him, glorified is He, and which are the necessary consequence of His names and attributes.

If you understand the secret of this aspect, well and good; otherwise pass over it to what precedes it, and do not hasten to deny it.

The secret of the matter is this: He, the Wise, the Merciful, creates only with wisdom and mercy. So when He punishes whoever He punishes for a wisdom, this proceeds in accordance with that wisdom, just as there exist in this world legal and divine punishments that carry refinement, discipline, deterrence, mercy, and gentleness, which purify souls, cleanse them, refine them, and free them from their evil and filth. Evil and wicked souls, which if they were returned to the world before the punishment would revert to what they were forbidden, are not fit to dwell in the Abode of Peace, which is incompatible with lying, evil, and injustice. So when such souls are punished with the Fire, with a punishment that frees them from that evil and removes their filth, this is judged reasonable in wisdom, just as is found in the punishments of this world. The creation of one in whom there is evil that is removed by punishment belongs to the completeness of wisdom.

As for creating souls of evil whose evil never ceases at all, and which were created for pure evil and everlasting torment that lasts as long as their Creator, glorified is He, this does not appear to accord with wisdom and mercy. Even if it falls under His power, its falling under wisdom and mercy is not clear. This is where inquiry has reached in this matter, in which the minds of the intelligent falter. I had asked Shaykh al-Islam, may God sanctify his spirit, about it, and he said to me: "This question is great and grave," and he did not answer it with anything. A time passed until I saw in the Tafsir of Abd ibn Humayd (al-Kashshi) some of those reports I had mentioned. I sent him the book while he was in his last session, marked that passage, and said to the messenger: "Tell him this passage is troubling to him, and he does not know what it is."

He wrote on it, in his well-known work, may God have mercy on him: "Whoever has abundant knowledge, let him inform him, for above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing."

I, in this matter, follow the statement of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, for he mentioned the entry of the people of Paradise into Paradise and of the people of the Fire into the Fire, and described that in the finest description, then said: "And God does after that with His creation what He wills."

And I follow the view of Abdullah ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with both of them, where he says: "It is not fitting for anyone to pass judgment on God regarding His creation, nor to cause them to descend into Paradise or into the Fire," and he mentioned this in explaining His words: ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode, wherein you shall abide forever, except as God wills﴾.

And I follow the view of Abu Said al-Khudri, where he says: "The whole Qur'an ends at this verse: ﴿Indeed your Lord is the Accomplisher of what He intends﴾."

And I follow the view of Qatadah, where he says, regarding His words ﴿except as your Lord wills﴾: "God knows best its clarification, as it has occurred."

And I follow the view of Ibn Zayd, where he says: "God has informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise." Ata said: "(not cut off) — but He has not informed us of what He wills for the people of the Fire."

The claim that the Fire and its punishment are everlasting as long as God is everlasting is a report about God regarding what He does. If it does not agree with His report about Himself concerning that, then it is speaking about Him without knowledge. The texts do not indicate that, and God knows best.

**(Section)**

There are other false doctrines here, among them the view of those who say that they are punished in the Fire for a period equal to their lifetime in this world; the view of those who say that a fiery nature will be transformed upon them so that they find pleasure in it, as the mangy person finds pleasure in scratching; and the view of those who say that both the Fire and Paradise will perish and return to nothingness; and the view of those who say that its movements will cease and its people will remain in permanent stillness. None succeeded in reaching the truth in this matter except the Companions and those who followed their path. And success is from God.

He said in *Hadi al-Arwah* (The Guide to the Souls):

**[Chapter Sixty-Seven: On the Eternity of Paradise, and that it does not perish or cease to exist]**

This is among what is known necessarily, that the Messenger of God ﷺ reported it. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿As for those who are made happy, they shall abide in Paradise forever, as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills — a gift without end﴾.

That is, uncut off. There is no contradiction between this and His words ﴿except as your Lord wills﴾.

The early scholars differed regarding this exception.

Ma'mar reported from al-Dahhak that it concerns those who come out of the Fire and enter Paradise. God, the Exalted, says that they abide forever in Paradise as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except for the period of their stay in the Fire.

I say: This allows two possibilities. The first is that the report about those who are made happy refers to a specific group, namely these people. The second, which is the more evident, is that it refers to the whole body of the blessed, and the specification by those mentioned is within the exception and what it indicates. Better than these two interpretations is to return the will (exception) to all of them, insofar as they were not in Paradise at the place of standing. On this view, no specification remains in the verse.

Another group said: it is an exception that the Lord, exalted is He, made but does not carry out, as you say: "By God, I will strike you, unless I see otherwise," while you do not see otherwise, but rather you are certain of striking him.

Another group said: when the Arabs make an exception of a large quantity along with its like and along with what is greater than it, the meaning of "illa" (except) in that case is the same as the meaning of "wa" (and). The meaning according to this is: apart from what God wills of the addition beyond the duration of the heavens and the earth.

This is the view of al-Farra'. Sibawayh makes "illa" mean "lakin" (but). They said that an analogy of this is that you say: "I owe you a thousand, except the two thousand before it," meaning: apart from the two thousand.

Ibn Jarir said: "This is the more beloved of the two views to me, since God does not break His promise, and the exception is connected to His words ﴿a gift without end﴾."

They said: an analogy of this is that you say: "I have lodged you in my house for a year, except for what you wish," meaning: apart from what you wish, or but what you wish of the addition to it.

Another group said: this exception refers only to the period of their confinement away from Paradise between death and resurrection, in the intermediate state (barzakh), until they arrive at Paradise. Then there is eternal abiding. So they were absent from Paradise only for the duration of their stay in the intermediate state.

Another group said: the resolute decree was given to them by God, that they abide forever until God wills otherwise, informing them that they abide forever within His will. This is like what He said to His Prophet: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away what We have revealed to you﴾, and His words ﴿If God wills, He would seal your heart﴾, and His words ﴿Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you﴾, and their like.

He, glorified is He, informed His servants that all matters are by His will: what God wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur.

Another group said: the intended meaning of the duration of the heavens and the earth is in this world. God, the Exalted, informed that they abide forever in Paradise for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what God wills of addition to it beyond that.

Perhaps this is the view of those who say that "illa" means "siwa" (apart from), though their expression differs.

This is the choice of Ibn Qutaybah. He said: the meaning is: "abiding therein for the duration of the world, apart from what He wills to add to them of abiding beyond the duration of the world." Another group said: "ma" means "man" (who), as in His words ﴿marry what is good for you of women﴾. The meaning is: except whoever your Lord wills to cause to enter the Fire for his sins, from among the blessed.

The difference between this view and the first views is that the exception on this view concerns the duration, while on that view it concerns the persons.

Another group said: the intended meaning of the heavens and the earth is the heaven of Paradise and its earth, and both abide forever.

His words ﴿except as your Lord wills, indeed your Lord﴾: if "ma" means "man," they are those who enter the Fire and then leave it. If "ma" means a period of time, then it is the duration of their confinement in the intermediate state and at the place of standing.

Al-Ja'fi said: "I asked Abdullah ibn Wahb about this exception, and he said: I heard about it that it is the duration of their standing at the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection until He judges between the people."

Another group said: the exception refers to the duration of their stay in this world.

These views are close to one another, and it is possible to reconcile them by saying: God informed that they abide forever in Paradise at every time, except a time in which He wills that they not be in it. This includes their time in this world, in the intermediate state, at the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, on the Bridge (sirat), and the presence of some of them in the Fire for a period. In every case, this verse is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses.

His words in it ﴿a gift without end﴾ are clear (muhkam), and likewise His words ﴿They wish to come out of the Fire, but they shall not come out of it﴾, and His words ﴿Indeed this is Our provision, which has no end﴾, and His words ﴿Its food is everlasting and its shade﴾, and His words ﴿And they shall not be brought out from it﴾.

God, the Exalted, has affirmed the eternal abiding of the people of Paradise in several places in the Qur'an, and informed that they ﴿taste therein no death except the first death﴾.

This exception is disjunctive (munqati'), and if you join it to the exception in His words ﴿except as your Lord wills﴾, the meaning of the two verses becomes clear to you.

The exception of the time in which they were not in Paradise from the duration of their abiding is like the exception of the first death from the totality of death. That death preceded their eternal life, and this departure from Paradise preceded their abiding in it. And success is from God.

The saying of the Prophet ﷺ has already passed: "Whoever enters Paradise will be blessed and will not despair, will abide and will not die."

And his saying: "A herald will call out: O people of Paradise, you shall be healthy and never fall ill, you shall be young and never grow old, you shall live and never die."

And it is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Said al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Death will be brought in the form of a horned ram, and it will be stopped between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise! They will look up fearfully. And it will be said: O people of the Fire! They will look up joyfully. It will be asked: Do you recognize this? They will say: Yes, this is death. It will be slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, eternity without death! And O people of the Fire, eternity without death!"

**(Section)**

This is a matter over which the later scholars differed into three views:

The first: that Paradise and the Fire are both perishable, not everlasting, but like their being created, they are perishable.

The second: that both are enduring and everlasting, never perishing.

The third: that Paradise is enduring and everlasting, while the Fire is perishable.

We will mention these views, what opposes them, the arguments advanced by the proponents of each view, and we will reject whatever contradicts the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ.

As for the view that both will perish, it is the view held by Jahm ibn Safwan, the leader of the Jahmiyyah, the deniers of divine attributes. No predecessor of his held it, neither among the Companions nor among the Successors, nor any of the leaders of Islam, nor did anyone among the people of the Sunnah hold it.

This view is one that the leaders of Islam denounced against him and his followers, declared them disbelievers for it, and cried out against them from every corner of the earth. This is what Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad reported in the *Kitab al-Sunnah* from Kharijah ibn Mus'ab, who said: "The Jahmiyyah disbelieved on account of three verses of the Book of God, the Mighty and Majestic: God's words ﴿its food is everlasting and its shade﴾, and they say it is not everlasting; and God's words ﴿Indeed this is Our provision, which has no end﴾, and they say it has an end; and God's words, the Mighty and Majestic ﴿What is with you comes to an end, but what is with God endures﴾."

Shaykh al-Islam said: "This was said by Jahm because of his foundational belief, which is the impossibility of the existence of an infinite series of temporal events. They made this their main proof for the createdness of the world. Jahm held that whatever prevents an infinite series of events in the past also prevents it in the future, just as it is impossible for him in the past. Abu al-Hudhayl al-Allaf, the shaykh of the Mu'tazilah, agreed with him on this principle, but said: this entails the perishing of movements, since they succeed one another, one after another. So he held that the movements of the people of Paradise and the Fire will perish, until they come to a permanent stillness in which none of them can move."

A group that agreed with them on the impossibility of an endless series of events claimed that this view is required by reason, but that when revelation came declaring the enduring of Paradise and the Fire, they affirmed that. These people did not realize that what is impossible in reason cannot be reported in revelation as occurring, since it would be impossible for Him to inform of the existence of what is impossible in reason. It seems they did not distinguish between the impossibilities of reason and what is beyond reason. Revelation comes with the second, not the first. Revelation brings what reason is unable to grasp and cannot independently establish, and does not bring what reason knows to be impossible.

Most of those who agreed with Jahm and Abu al-Hudhayl on this principle distinguished between the past and the future. They said: the past has already entered existence, unlike the future. What is impossible is that an infinite quantity enter existence, not that its entry be supposed one after another. They said: these are two analogies. One says: "I will not give you a dirham except that I will give you another dirham after it," and this is possible. The first analogy is: "I will not give you a dirham except that I gave you one before it," and this is impossible. These people hold that the existence of an infinite series in the past is impossible, while its existence in the future is necessary.

Others disputed this with them, saying: "Rather, the matter in the past is the same as in the future. There is no difference between them. The past and the future are relative matters. Everything that will be future becomes past, and everything past was once future. Therefore it is not rational to affirm the possibility of perpetuity at one end and its impossibility at the other." They said: "This is a question of the perpetuity of the Lord's action, blessed and exalted is He. He has always been Lord, capable, and an agent, for He has always been living, knowing, powerful. It is impossible that the act should be impossible for Him by His essence, and then turn into possibility for Him by His essence without any renewal of anything. Eternity has no limit that would make the act possible for Him at a certain point while it was impossible for Him before it. The view that this entails is clear enough to establish its corruption. It suffices to refute it that the moment at which the act changed from essential impossibility to essential possibility either can be supposed to have had a prior time in which the act was possible, or not. If you say it cannot, this is an arbitrary and unintelligible claim, of the kind of madness. If you say it can, then it is said: likewise, whatever is supposed before it, without end. For no time, real or assumed, exists in which the act is not possible for Him, and it is a quality of perfection, goodness, and the object of the praise, lordship, and dominion of the Lord, who has always been Lord, praiseworthy, King, capable, and these attributes have not newly come to Him, just as He has always been living, willing, and knowing. Life, will, knowledge, and power require their effects and objects. How is it conceivable that a living, powerful, knowing, willing being, with nothing preventing him and no one overpowering him, should be impossible for him to do anything at all? How can this be made a principle of religion and a standard for what God and His Messenger reported, and by which one distinguishes the permissible from the impossible in reason? If this is the standard, and this is the nature of the scale, how can what is weighed by it be correct?"

As for the view of those who distinguish that the past has entered existence while the future has not, it is a statement with no real substance behind it. What existence contains of movements is finite, and then it ceases and becomes past, just as it was nonexistent when it was future. Its existence is between two nonexistences. Whenever one whole passes, another whole comes after it. What has become past is the very thing that was future. If the proof establishes the impossibility of an infinite series before one thing, it equally establishes its impossibility after one thing.

As for your distinction, by saying that the future is like the statement "I will not give you a dirham except that I will give you another after it," which is possible, and the past is like the statement "I will not give you a dirham except that I will give you one before it," which is impossible: this distinction is an obvious deception. It is not an analogy to what we are discussing. Its analogue is rather to say: "I will not give you a dirham except that I have already given you a dirham before it." This is possible in perpetuity for the past, within the same limits as its possibility for the future. There is no difference between them at all in sound reason.

Since Jahm, Abu al-Hudhayl, and their followers did not find any difference between the two matters, they held that the movements must have a finite end in the future, just as their beginning is necessary in the past according to them.

The Ahl al-Hadith said: rather, both are equal in possibility and in occurrence. The Lord, glorified and exalted, has never ceased to be one who does what He wills, and He has never ceased, and does not cease, to be described by attributes of perfection and named by names of majesty. He is not like one who is able to act at all times, as opposed to one who can act only at a specific time. Nor is one who creates like one who does not create, nor one who does good like one who does not do good, nor one who governs the affair like one who does not govern. What perfection is there in the Lord of the worlds being rendered inactive from acting for a determined or defined period, or for an endless duration, so that action becomes impossible for Him? The reality of this is that He is not able to do it. And if you refuse this unqualified statement and say that the impossible cannot be described as "not within His power," then you have combined two impossibilities: ruling that the act is permissible without any reason that makes it impossible, and transforming it from an essential impossibility into an essential possibility without any renewed cause. You also claim that this is the foundation by which you establish the existence of the Creator, the origination of the world, and the sustaining of bodies. In doing so you have harmed the intellect, the Sharia, and the Lord, may He be exalted. He has never ceased to be capable of acting and speaking by His will, has never ceased to be one who does what He wills, and has never ceased to be a Lord who does good.

The point is that the claim that Paradise and Hell will perish is an innovation (bid'ah) that no one among the Companions, the Successors, or any of the Imams of the Muslims has said. Those who said it took it from a corrupt analogy, the basis of which became confused for many people, so they believed it to be true and built upon it the doctrine of the createdness of the Qur'an and the negation of the attributes. The Qur'an, the Sunnah, and sound reason all indicate that the words and actions of Allah do not come to an end, are not cut off by a last, and are not bounded by a first. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement.﴾ And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens and the sea, with seven more seas to replenish it, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Almighty and Wise.﴾

So He informed that His words are not exhausted, because of His might and His wisdom, and these are two essential attributes of His, glorified and exalted; He is not otherwise.

Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned in his tafsir, from Sulayman ibn Amir, who said: I heard al-Rabi' ibn Anas say: The likeness of all the knowledge of the servants in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is like a drop from all these seas. And Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed concerning this: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens...﴾ the verse. And His saying: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink...﴾ the verse.

He, glorified and exalted, says: Say: If the sea were ink for the words of Allah, and all the trees were pens, the pens would break and the water of the sea would run out, while the words of Allah, may He be exalted, remain; nothing can exhaust them, because no one can measure His measure or praise Him as He deserves. Rather, He is as He praised Himself: "Indeed, our Lord, as He says, and beyond what He says." Then, the delight of this world, its beginning and its end, compared with the delight of the Hereafter, is like a grain of mustard in the whole expanse of the earth.

(Section)

As for the everlastingness and perpetuity of the Fire, Shaykh al-Islam said: concerning it there are two well-known opinions from the early generations and the later ones, and the dispute about it is well known among the Successors.

I say: here there are seven opinions.

The first: whoever enters it will never leave it, but everyone who enters it abides in it forever, by the permission of Allah. This is the view of the Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah.

The second: its people are punished in it for a period, then it turns against them, and a fiery nature remains for them, in which they take delight because it agrees with their nature. This is the view of the imam of the Ittihadiyyah, Ibn 'Arabi al-Ta'i, who said in his Fusus: "The praise is for the truthfulness of the promise, not the truthfulness of the threat. The Divine Presence seeks praise that is praiseworthy in its essence, so He is praised for the truthfulness of His promise, not the truthfulness of His threat, but rather for overlooking. So do not think that Allah breaks His promise to His messengers," and He did not say "His threat," but said: "and He overlooks their evil deeds," even though He threatened that, and praised Isma'il for being "true to his promise." Possibility has been removed from the right of the Real, because of what it contains of seeking a preponderant side:

"There remains none but the one true to the promise alone, and for the threat of the Real there is no visible eye.
And if they enter the abode of wretchedness, they are upon a pleasure within which is a separate bliss.
The bliss of the gardens of eternity, and the matter is one, and between them at the time of unveiling there is a difference.
It is called punishment because of the sweetness of its taste, and that is for it like the husk, and the husk is separate."

This is at one extreme. The Mu'tazilah, who say that it is not permissible for Allah to break His threat, rather it is obligatory for Him to punish whom He threatened with punishment, are at the other extreme.

For those [Mu'tazilah], no one of the Muslims escapes the Fire once he has entered it at all. For this one [Ibn 'Arabi], no one is punished in it at all. Both groups oppose what is known by necessity: that the Messenger came with it and reported it from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The third: the view of the one who says that its people are punished in it until a set time, then they come out of it, and others come after them to take their place in it.

This view was reported to the Prophet by the Jews, and he refuted them regarding it, and Allah refuted them in the Qur'an. He said: ﴿And they said: The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days. Say: Have you taken a covenant with Allah? For Allah will not break His covenant. Or do you say about Allah what you do not know?﴾ And He said: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, being called to the Book of Allah so that it may judge between them, and then a faction of them turns away while they are refusing? That is because they said: The Fire will not touch us except for numbered days, and what they used to fabricate has deceived them in their religion.﴾ So this view is only the view of the enemies of Allah, the Jews, who are the elders of its adherents and those who say it. The Qur'an, the Sunnah, the consensus of the Companions, the Successors, and the Imams of Islam indicate its corruption. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿They will not be removed from the Fire﴾; and He said: ﴿They will not be removed﴾; and He said: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it from distress, they will be returned to it﴾; and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Every time they wish to come out of it, they will be returned into it﴾; and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾; and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle.﴾

This is the most eloquent statement that can be made about the impossibility of their entering Paradise.

The fourth: the view of one who says they will come out of it while it remains as a fire in its state with no one in it being punished. Shaykh al-Islam reported this view.

The Qur'an and the Sunnah also refute this view, as has been mentioned.

The fifth: the view of one who says rather it will perish by itself, because it is something created after it was not, and whatever is proven to have come into being is impossible to remain or be everlasting. This is the view of Jahm ibn Safwan and his followers, and for him there is no difference in that between Paradise and the Fire.

The sixth: the view of one who says their life and movements will perish, and they will become inanimate, not moving and not feeling pain. This is the view of Abu al-Hudhayl al-'Allaf, the imam of the Mu'tazilah, by extension from the impossibility of an endless series of events; and for him Paradise and the Fire are equal in this ruling.

The seventh: the view of one who says rather its Lord and Creator, blessed and exalted, will annihilate it, for He has set for it a term at which it ends, and then it will perish and its punishment will cease.

Shaykh al-Islam said: This view has been reported from 'Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id, and others. 'Abd ibn Humayd, who is among the greatest imams of hadith, reported in his well-known tafsir: "Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Thabit, from al-Hasan, who said: 'Umar said: If the people of the Fire remained in the Fire as many as the grains of 'Aalij sand, there would still be a day for them on which they would come out.'"

And he said: "Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: If the people of the Fire remained in the Fire as many as the grains of 'Aalij sand, there would still be a day for them on which they would come out of it." He mentioned this in the tafsir of His saying: ﴿remaining in it for ages (ahqab)﴾.

'Abd, who is among the imams and memorizers and scholars of the Sunnah, reported it from these two eminent men, Sulayman ibn Harb and Hajjaj ibn Minhal, and both of them from Hammad ibn Salamah, and that is enough for its prestige. Hammad narrated it from Thabit and Humayd, and both of them narrate it from al-Hasan, and this chain is enough for its eminence. Al-Hasan, although he did not hear it from 'Umar, narrated it from some of the Successors; and if it were not authentic to him from 'Umar, he would not have stated it definitively. And 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said... Even if it is assumed that it was not preserved from 'Umar, the transmission of these imams of it, without opposing it or rejecting it, along with their condemnation of whoever opposes the Sunnah even without this, indicates that if this view were, to these imams, one of the innovations opposing the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, and the consensus of the imams, they would have been the first to denounce it.

He said: There is no doubt that whoever stated this view from 'Umar and transmitted it from him meant by it the category of the people of the Fire who are its people. As for people who were afflicted because of their sins, these and others know that they will come out of it, and that they will not remain there for the duration of the grains of 'Aalij sand or anything close to it. And the term "the people of the Fire" is not restricted to the monotheists, but is restricted to those other than them, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "As for the people of the Fire, who are its people, they will neither die in it nor live."

This is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾ and His saying: ﴿and they will not be removed from it﴾. Rather, what Allah has reported is the truth and the reality whose opposite does not occur. But when its term has ended and it perishes, and the world perishes, it will no longer be Fire and no punishment will remain in it.

The proponents of this view said: In the tafsir of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿He said: The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing﴾, he said: It is not fitting for anyone to pass judgment on Allah concerning His creation, nor to make them enter Paradise or Fire.

They said: This threat in this verse is not restricted to the people of the qiblah, for He, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿And on the day He gathers them all: O assembly of jinn, you have taken much from mankind. And their allies from mankind will say: Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us. He will say: The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing. Thus We will make some wrongdoers allies of others, for what they used to earn.﴾ The allies of the jinn among mankind definitely include the disbelievers, for they have more right to be their allies than the disobedient Muslims, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who make him an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from the devil touches them, remember, and at once they are seeing clearly. But their brothers [the devils] extend them in error, then they do not restrain﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿So fight the allies of Satan﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers﴾; and He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, the devils inspire to their allies to dispute with you; and if you obey them, you would indeed be associators﴾. And the exception occurred in the verse that informed about the entry of the allies of the devils into the Fire.

From here Ibn 'Abbas said: It is not fitting for anyone to pass judgment on Allah concerning His creation. They said: The view of the one who says that "illa" (except) means "siwa" (other than), i.e., other than what Allah wills to increase for them of kinds of punishment and its time, its contrariness to what is excepted and what is excepted from is not hidden, and what the addressee understands is the opposition of what follows "illa" to what precedes it.

They said: And the view of the one who says that it is for excluding the time before their entry into it, such as the time of the barzakh and the place of standing and the duration of the world as well, the wording does not support it, for it is an exception from a declarative sentence whose content is that when they enter the Fire they will remain in it for the duration of the heavens and the earth, except what Allah wills. And the intended meaning is not an exception before entry; this is what the addressee does not understand. Do you not see that He, glorified, addresses them with this in the Fire, when they say: "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us," and He then says to them: "The Fire is your abode, abiding therein, except as Allah wills."

In His saying: ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another, and we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾ there is a kind of acknowledgment, submission, and regret. That is: the jinn benefited from us and we benefited from them, so we shared in shirk and its causes and its means, and we preferred enjoyment over Your obedience and the obedience of Your messengers; our terms ended and our lives passed in that, and we did not earn in them Your pleasure, and the ultimate outcome of our term was only that some of us benefited from others. So reflect on what this statement contains of acknowledgment of the reality of what they were upon, and how that reality became evident to them on that day, and they knew that what they were in during their terms was their share of enjoying one another, and they did not enjoy the worship of their Lord, His knowledge, His oneness, His love, and preferring His pleasure. This is of the same kind as their saying: ﴿If we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze﴾; and His saying: ﴿So they acknowledged their sin﴾; and His saying: ﴿So they knew that the truth belongs to Allah﴾; and their parallels.

The point is that His saying: ﴿except as Allah wills﴾ refers to these mentioned people, either exclusively to them or inclusively to them and to the disobedient monotheists. As for its being restricted to the disobedient Muslims apart from these, there is no basis for that.

When a group saw the weakness of this view, they said: The exception refers to the duration of the barzakh and the place of standing, and the weakness of this view has been made clear. Another group saw that the exception refers to another kind of punishment other than the Fire.
